claims.statement: Loong belongs to Chinese mythology and commonly has a serpentine shape with four legs.
claims.statement_id: Loong adalah naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok, lazim digambarkan menyerupai ular dengan empat kaki.
claims.quote: The Chinese dragon, known as long or loong (/lʊŋ/ LUUNG) is a legendary creature in Chinese mythology, Chinese folklore, and Chinese culture generally. Chinese dragons have many animal-like forms, such as turtles and fish, but are most commonly depicted as snake-like with four legs.

claims.statement: The dragon served as an emblem of imperial authority in Chinese history.
claims.statement_id: Naga menjadi lambang kekuasaan kaisar dalam sejarah Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Historically, the Chinese dragon was associated with the emperor of China and used as a symbol to represent imperial power. Liu Bang, the founder of the Han dynasty, claimed that he was conceived after his mother dreamt of a dragon. During the Tang dynasty, emperors wore robes with dragon motif as an imperial symbol, and high officials might also be presented with dragon robes.

claims.statement: Coiled dragon forms occur on jade amulets from the Shang period.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk naga melingkar juga ditemukan pada amulet giok zaman Shang.
claims.quote: The coiled dragon or snake form played an important role in early Chinese culture. The character for "dragon" in the earliest Chinese writing has a similar coiled form, as do later jade dragon amulets from the Shang period.

claims.statement: Scientific examination identifies many objects called dragon bones as mammal fossils.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian benda yang dahulu disebut tulang naga ternyata fosil mamalia.
claims.quote: Scientific examination of "dragon bones" from the 19th century to the present suggests they most commonly are remains of fossil Cenozoic mammals, such as the extinct horse Hipparion.

claims.statement: Wang Fu recorded a tradition of nine animal resemblances in dragon anatomy.
claims.statement_id: Wang Fu mencatat tradisi sembilan kemiripan anatomi naga dengan hewan lain.
claims.quote: From its origins as totems or the stylized depiction of natural creatures, the Chinese dragon evolved to become a mythical animal. The Han dynasty scholar Wang Fu recorded Chinese myths that long dragons had nine anatomical resemblances.

claims.statement: Doré records an anatomical variant with deer antlers and a crocodile head.
claims.statement_id: Doré mencatat varian anatomi dengan tanduk rusa dan kepala buaya.
claims.quote: "The antlers of a deer. The head of a crocodile. A demon's eyes. The neck of a snake. A tortoise's viscera. A hawk's claws. The palms of a tiger. A cow's ears. And it hears through its horns, its ears being deprived of all power of hearing".

claims.statement: Art often shows dragons pursuing or contesting a flaming pearl.
claims.statement_id: Naga dalam seni sering mengejar atau memperebutkan mutiara menyala.
claims.quote: Many pictures of Chinese dragons show a flaming pearl under their chin or in their claws. The pearl is associated with spiritual energy, wisdom, prosperity, power, immortality, thunder, or the moon. Chinese art often depicts a pair of dragons chasing or fighting over a flaming pearl.

claims.statement: Popular belief connects dragons with rivers, seas, and the distribution of rain.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan populer menghubungkan naga dengan sungai, laut, dan pengaturan hujan.
claims.quote: Chinese dragons are strongly associated with water and weather in popular religion. They are believed to be the rulers of moving bodies of water, such as waterfalls, rivers, or seas. The Dragon god is the dispenser of rain as well as the zoomorphic representation of yang, the masculine power of generation.

claims.statement: During drought or flooding, villagers offered sacrifices and religious rites to appease local dragon kings and seek rain.
claims.statement_id: Saat kekeringan atau banjir, masyarakat melakukan ritual untuk memohon bantuan raja naga setempat.
claims.quote: Because of this association, they are seen as "in charge" of water-related weather phenomena. In premodern times, many Chinese villages (especially those close to rivers and seas) had temples dedicated to their local "dragon king".

claims.statement: One legend describes the Yellow Emperor ascending to heaven after becoming a dragon.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah legenda mengisahkan Kaisar Kuning naik ke langit setelah menjadi naga.
claims.quote: According to Chinese legend, both Chinese primogenitors, the earliest Door and the Yellow Emperor, were closely related to the dragon. At the end of his reign, the first legendary ruler, the Yellow Emperor, was said to have been immortalized into a dragon that resembled his emblem, and ascended to Heaven.

claims.statement: The Norton Museum describes dragons as heavenly rulers petitioned for rain through ritual.
claims.statement_id: Museum Norton menjelaskan naga sebagai penguasa langit yang dimohon mendatangkan hujan dalam ritual.
claims.quote: Each work depicts dragons, the heavenly sovereigns, petitioned to bring rain in ritual ceremonies.

claims.statement: On court robes, dragon imagery refers to the emperor’s mandate to rule from the Dragon Throne.
claims.statement_id: Pada jubah istana, naga merujuk pada mandat kaisar untuk memerintah dari Takhta Naga.
claims.quote: The presence of dragons on the robes refers to the emperor holding the Mandate of Heaven to rule from the Dragon Throne.

claims.statement: The V&A interprets the flaming pearl in dragon imagery as wisdom, enlightenment, and spiritual essence.
claims.statement_id: Museum V&A menafsirkan mutiara menyala dalam motif naga sebagai kebijaksanaan, pencerahan, dan hakikat spiritual.
claims.quote: It is highly unlikely the decorator of this object knew that the image depicts the Chinese legend of the Dragon pursuing the ‘Flaming Pearl’ representing wisdom, enlightenment and spiritual essence.

claims.statement: Dragon patterns on Chinese export ceramics inspired British printed blue-and-white wares in the nineteenth century.
claims.statement_id: Pola naga pada keramik ekspor Tiongkok mengilhami keramik cetak biru-putih Inggris abad kesembilan belas.
claims.quote: Popularity of these export wares continued into the 19th century when British production of printed blue and white ceramics drew inspiration from the Asian patterns.

claims.statement: The V&A notes that the British plate pattern follows blue-and-white porcelain exported from China in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
claims.statement_id: V&A mencatat bahwa pola piring Inggris mengikuti porselen biru-putih yang diekspor dari Tiongkok pada abad ketujuh belas dan kedelapan belas.
claims.quote: The design for the bowl is based on a type of hand-painted blue-and-white porcelain that was widely exported from China to Asia and Europe in the 17th and 18th centuries, as you can see with the following example made in Jingdezhen, 1700-1710.

claims.statement: In Chinese mythology, Nüwa is a goddess associated with humanity's creation.
claims.statement_id: Nüwa adalah dewi pencipta manusia dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Nüwa, also read Nügua, is a mother goddess, culture hero, and/or member of the Three Sovereigns of Chinese mythology. She is a goddess in Chinese folk religion, Chinese Buddhism, Confucianism and Taoism. She is credited with creating humanity and repairing the Pillar of Heaven.

claims.statement: A creation account describes her shaping people from yellow clay.
claims.statement_id: Kisah penciptaan menggambarkannya membentuk manusia dengan tanah liat kuning.
claims.quote: As creator of mankind, she molded humans individually by hand with yellow clay. In other stories where she fulfills this role, she only created nobles and/or the rich out of yellow soil. The stories vary on the other details about humanity's creation, but it was a tradition commonly believed in ancient China that she created commoners from brown mud.

claims.statement: Another version distinguishes hand-shaped people from those made using a muddy cord.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain membedakan manusia yang dibentuk tangan dan manusia yang dibuat melalui tali berlumpur.
claims.quote: A story holds that she was tired when she created "the rich and the noble", so all others, or "cord-made people", were created from her "dragg[ing] a string through mud".

claims.statement: In the Huainanzi account, she repairs the damaged sky using stones of five colors.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Huainanzi, ia menambal langit yang rusak dengan batu lima warna.
claims.quote: In the Huainanzi, there is a description of a great battle between deities that broke the pillars supporting Heaven and caused great devastation. There was great flooding, and Heaven had collapsed. Nüwa was the one who patched the holes in Heaven with five colored stones, and she used the legs of a tortoise to mend the pillars.

claims.statement: She also uses a tortoise's legs to restore the supports of heaven.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga menggunakan kaki kura-kura untuk menggantikan tiang penyangga langit.
claims.quote: In the Huainanzi, there is a description of a great battle between deities that broke the pillars supporting Heaven and caused great devastation. There was great flooding, and Heaven had collapsed. Nüwa was the one who patched the holes in Heaven with five colored stones, and she used the legs of a tortoise to mend the pillars.

claims.statement: One honorific identifies her as Wahuang, Empress Wa.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu gelar penghormatannya ialah Wahuang, Permaisuri Wa.
claims.quote: Her reverential name is Wahuang (媧皇; 'Empress Wa').

claims.statement: Werner presents Nue Kua Shih (also called Nue Wa and Nue Hsi) as the sister and successor of Fu Hsi, and as the creator of human beings when the earth first emerged from Chaos.
claims.statement_id: Werner menyebut Nue Kua Shih (juga disebut Nue Wa dan Nue Hsi) sebagai saudari sekaligus penerus Fu Hsi, dan sebagai pencipta manusia ketika bumi pertama kali muncul dari Kekacauan.
claims.quote: Nue Kua Shih (also called Nue Wa and Nue Hsi), said to have been the sister and successor of Fu Hsi, ... as having been the creator of human beings when the earth first emerged from Chaos.

claims.statement: Werner notes that the sex seems uncertain, that she is described with the body of a serpent and head of an ox (or a human head and ox horns according to some writers), and that she "moulded yellow earth and made man".
claims.statement_id: Werner mencatat bahwa jenis kelaminnya tampak tidak pasti, bahwa ia digambarkan bertubuh ular dan berkepala sapi (atau berkepala manusia dengan tanduk sapi menurut sebagian penulis), dan bahwa ia "membentuk tanah kuning dan membuat manusia".
claims.quote: She (or he, for the sex seems uncertain), who had the "body of a serpent and head of an ox" (or a human head and horns of an ox, according to some writers), "moulded yellow earth and made man."

claims.statement: In the account of Ssu-ma Cheng quoted by Werner, Nue Kua had the body of a serpent and a human head, with the virtuous endowments of a divine sage.
claims.statement_id: Dalam uraian Ssu-ma Cheng yang dikutip Werner, Nue Kua bertubuh ular dan berkepala manusia, dengan sifat-sifat utama seorang bijak ilahi.
claims.quote: Nue Kua had the body of a serpent and a human head, with the virtuous endowments of a divine sage.

claims.statement: Ssu-ma Cheng (quoted by Werner) relates that toward the end of her reign the feudatory prince Kung Kung struck his head against the Imperfect Mountain, Pu Chou Shan, bringing it down, so that the pillars of Heaven were broken and the corners of the earth gave way.
claims.statement_id: Ssu-ma Cheng (dikutip Werner) menceritakan bahwa menjelang akhir pemerintahannya, pangeran bawahan Kung Kung membenturkan kepalanya ke Gunung Pu Chou Shan hingga roboh, sehingga tiang-tiang Langit patah dan sudut-sudut bumi runtuh.
claims.quote: Toward the end of her reign there was among the feudatory princes Kung Kung ... he struck his head against the Imperfect Mountain, Pu Chou Shan, and brought it down. The pillars of Heaven were broken and the corners of the earth gave way.

claims.statement: In that account Nue Kua melted stones of the five colours to repair the heavens and cut off the feet of the tortoise to set upright the four extremities of the earth.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan itu, Nue Kua melebur batu lima warna untuk memperbaiki langit dan memotong kaki kura-kura untuk menegakkan keempat ujung bumi.
claims.quote: Hereupon Nue Kua melted stones of the five colours to repair the heavens, and cut off the feet of the tortoise to set upright the four extremities of the earth.

claims.statement: By gathering the ashes of reeds she stopped the flooding waters and so rescued the land of Chi, Chi Chou.
claims.statement_id: Dengan mengumpulkan abu alang-alang, ia menghentikan air bah dan dengan demikian menyelamatkan negeri Chi, Chi Chou.
claims.quote: Gathering the ashes of reeds she stopped the flooding waters, and thus rescued the land of Chi, Chi Chou

claims.statement: Another account recorded by Werner makes Nue and Kua brother and sister, the only two human beings in existence, placed at creation at the foot of the K'un-lun Mountains.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan lain yang dicatat Werner, Nue dan Kua adalah kakak beradik, satu-satunya dua manusia yang ada, yang pada saat penciptaan ditempatkan di kaki Pegunungan K'un-lun.
claims.quote: Another account separates the name and makes Nue and Kua brother and sister, describing them as the only two human beings in existence. At the creation they were placed at the foot of the K'un-lun Mountains.

claims.statement: Werner stresses that, as regards the heavens and the earth at least, she is regarded as the repairer and not the creator of them.
claims.statement_id: Werner menegaskan bahwa, setidaknya terhadap langit dan bumi, ia dipandang sebagai pemulih dan bukan pencipta.
claims.quote: as regards the heavens and the earth at least, she is regarded as the repairer and not the creator of them.

claims.statement: The Jade Emperor, also called Yudi, is a divine figure in Chinese myth and folk religion.
claims.statement_id: Jade Emperor atau Yudi merupakan tokoh ilahi dalam mitos dan agama rakyat Tiongkok.
claims.quote: In the myths and folk religion of Chinese culture, the Jade Emperor or Yudi is one of the representations of the primordial god.

claims.statement: Taoist theology places him in an assisting role to Yuanshi Tianzun.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teologi Tao, ia ditempatkan sebagai pembantu Yuanshi Tianzun.
claims.quote: In Taoist theology, he is the assistant of Yuanshi Tianzun, who is one of the Three Pure Ones, the three primordial emanations of the Tao. However, some Taoists in history were skeptical of his benevolence because his buildings and infrastructure in heaven and earth were sometimes seen as interfering with the many natural laws or dao.

claims.statement: Chinese Buddhist cosmology sometimes equates him with Śakra.
claims.statement_id: Kosmologi Buddhis Tiongkok kadang menyamakannya dengan Śakra.
claims.quote: He is often identified with Śakra in Chinese Buddhist cosmology and identified with Yu the Great in Chinese mythology.

claims.statement: His titles include Tiangong and Yu Huang Shangdi.
claims.statement_id: Gelar yang dipakai antara lain Tiangong dan Yu Huang Shangdi.
claims.quote: The Jade Emperor is known by many names, including Yu; Heavenly Grandfather (Chinese: 天公, romanized: Tiāngōng), which originally meant "Heavenly Duke" (and which is used by commoners); the Jade Lord; the Highest Emperor; and Great Emperor of Jade (玉皇上帝, Yu Huang Shangdi, or 玉皇大帝, Yu Huang Dadi).

claims.statement: An origin tale portrays him as a crown prince whose birth emits extraordinary light.
claims.statement_id: Kisah asal-usul menggambarkannya sebagai putra mahkota yang memancarkan cahaya saat lahir.
claims.quote: It was said that Jade Emperor was originally the crown prince of the kingdom of Pure Felicity and Majestic Heavenly Lights and Ornaments. At birth, he emitted a wondrous light that filled the entire kingdom. When he was young, he was kind, intelligent and wise.

claims.statement: One myth recounts how the Jade Emperor became monarch of the deities in heaven.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu mitos menceritakan bagaimana ia menjadi penguasa para dewa di langit.
claims.quote: One of the myths describes how the Jade Emperor became the monarch of all the deities in heaven. It is one of the few myths in which the Jade Emperor shows his power.

claims.statement: Werner writes that Yue Huang means "the Jade Emperor" or "the Pure August One", jade symbolizing purity, and that he is also known as Yue-huang Shang-ti, "the Pure August Emperor on High".
claims.statement_id: Werner menulis bahwa Yue Huang berarti "Kaisar Giok" atau "Yang Murni Agung", dengan giok melambangkan kemurnian; ia juga dikenal sebagai Yue-huang Shang-ti, "Kaisar Murni Agung di Atas".
claims.quote: Yue Huang means 'the Jade Emperor,' or 'the Pure August One,' jade symbolizing purity. He is also known by the name Yue-huang Shang-ti, 'the Pure August Emperor on High.'

claims.statement: In the legend of Yue Huang recorded by Werner, an ancient kingdom named Kuang Yen Miao Lo Kuo had a king called Ching Te and a queen called Pao Yueeh.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda Yue Huang yang dicatat Werner, pada zaman kuno ada kerajaan bernama Kuang Yen Miao Lo Kuo dengan raja Ching Te dan permaisuri Pao Yueeh.
claims.quote: The legend of Yue Huang relates that in ancient times there existed a kingdom named Kuang Yen Miao Lo Kuo, whose king was Ching Te, his queen being called Pao Yueeh.

claims.statement: In Werner's version, after his father's death the prince took the throne but abdicated after a few days in favour of his chief minister and became a hermit at P'u-ming in Shensi and on Mount Hsiu Yen in Yuennan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Werner, setelah ayahnya wafat sang pangeran naik takhta tetapi hanya beberapa hari kemudian turun demi menteri utamanya dan menjadi pertapa di P'u-ming di Shensi serta di Gunung Hsiu Yen di Yuennan.
claims.quote: On the death of his father he ascended the throne, but after reigning only a few days abdicated in favour of his chief minister, and became a hermit at P'u-ming, in Shensi, and also on Mount Hsiu Yen, in Yuennan.

claims.statement: Werner notes that both Buddhists and Taoists claim Yue Huang; the Buddhists identify him with Indra, in which case he is a Buddhist deity incorporated into the Taoist pantheon.
claims.statement_id: Werner mencatat bahwa umat Buddha dan Tao sama-sama mengklaim Yue Huang; umat Buddha menyamakannya dengan Indra, sehingga ia dipandang sebagai dewa Buddhis yang dimasukkan ke panteon Tao.
claims.quote: Both Buddhists and Taoists claim him as their own, the former identifying him with Indra, in which case Yue Huang is a Buddhist deity incorporated into the Taoist pantheon.

claims.statement: Werner begins his historical account with the Emperor Ch'eng Tsung of the Sung dynasty, who in A.D. 1005 was obliged to sign a peace with the Tunguses or Kitans.
claims.statement_id: Werner memulai uraian sejarahnya dengan Kaisar Ch'eng Tsung dari dinasti Sung, yang pada tahun 1005 M terpaksa menandatangani perdamaian dengan bangsa Tungus atau Kitan.
claims.quote: The history of this deity, who later received many honorific titles and became the most popular god, a very Chinese Jupiter, seems to be somewhat as follows: The Emperor Ch'eng Tsung of the Sung dynasty having been obliged in A.D. 1005 to sign a disgraceful peace with the Tunguses or Kitans

claims.statement: According to Werner, in the tenth moon of 1012 the emperor assembled his ministers and declared that in a dream an Immortal had brought him a letter from Yue Huang.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Werner, pada bulan kesepuluh tahun 1012 sang kaisar mengumpulkan para menterinya dan menyatakan bahwa dalam mimpi ia dikunjungi seorang Immortal yang membawa surat dari Yue Huang.
claims.quote: The Emperor, having studied his part well, assembled his ministers in the tenth moon of the year 1012, and made to them the following declaration: "In a dream I had a visit from an Immortal, who brought me a letter from Yue Huang

claims.statement: Werner interprets the cult of Yue Huang as originating in the emperor's announcement, which he calls a fraud; this is the author's interpretation, not the belief of its worshippers.
claims.statement_id: Werner menafsirkan bahwa pemujaan Yue Huang berawal dari pengumuman kaisar tersebut, yang ia sebut tipuan; ini tafsiran penulisnya, bukan keyakinan para pemujanya.
claims.quote: This is the origin of Yue Huang. He was born of a fraud, and came ready-made from the brain of an emperor.

claims.statement: Fenghuang are mythic birds found across traditions influenced by Chinese culture.
claims.statement_id: Fenghuang adalah burung mitologis yang dikenal dalam tradisi kawasan budaya Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Fenghuang (/fʌŋˈwɑːŋ/ fung-HWAHNG) are mythological birds featuring in traditions throughout the Sinosphere.

claims.statement: Fenghuang hold supremacy among birds and are often paired with dragons.
claims.statement_id: Fenghuang dianggap berkuasa atas burung lainnya dan sering dipasangkan dengan naga.
claims.quote: Fenghuang (/fʌŋˈwɑːŋ/ fung-HWAHNG) are mythological birds featuring in traditions throughout the Sinosphere.

claims.statement: Calling it a Chinese phoenix does not imply the same mythology as the Western phoenix.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan phoenix Tiongkok tidak berarti kisahnya sama dengan phoenix Barat.
claims.quote: In the West, they are commonly called Chinese phoenixes, although mythological similarities with the Western/Persian phoenix are superficial.

claims.statement: The Erya describes a composite anatomy including a rooster's beak and a snake's neck.
claims.statement_id: Erya menggambarkannya sebagai gabungan ciri berbagai hewan, termasuk paruh ayam dan leher ular.
claims.quote: A common depiction of fenghuang was of it attacking snakes with its talons and its wings spread. According to the Erya's chapter 17 Shiniao, fenghuang is made up of the beak of a rooster, the face of a swallow, the forehead of a fowl, the neck of a snake, the breast of a goose, the back of a tortoise, the hindquarters of a stag and the tail of a fish.

claims.statement: Its head, eyes, and back are associated with the sky, sun, and moon.
claims.statement_id: Kepala, mata, dan punggungnya dihubungkan dengan langit, matahari, dan bulan.
claims.quote: The fenghuang's body symbolizes the celestial bodies: the head is the sky, the eyes are the sun, the back is the moon, the wings are the wind, the feet are the earth, and the tail is the planets. The fenghuang is said to have originated in the sun. Its body contains the five fundamental colors: black, white, red, yellow, and green or blue.

claims.statement: One tradition locates its dwelling on Mount Danzuan in the southern mountains.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah tradisi menempatkan kediamannya di Gunung Danzuan di pegunungan selatan.
claims.quote: Chinese tradition cites it as living atop Mount Danzuan in the southern mountains.

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing (Nanshan jing) records a bird shaped like a chicken with a five-coloured pattern, named fenghuang (written 鳳皇); the pattern on its head is called de (virtue), on its wings yi, on its back li, on its breast ren, and on its belly xin.
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing (Nanshan jing) mencatat seekor burung berbentuk seperti ayam, berpola lima warna, bernama fenghuang (tertulis 鳳皇); pola kepalanya disebut "de" (kebajikan), sayapnya "yi", punggungnya "li", dadanya "ren", dan perutnya "xin".
claims.quote: 有鳥焉，其狀如雞，五采而文，名曰鳳皇，首文曰德，翼文曰義，背文曰禮，膺文曰仁，腹文曰信。

claims.statement: According to the Shanhaijing, this bird eats and drinks naturally, sings and dances of itself, and its appearance brings peace to the world.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Shanhaijing, burung ini makan dan minum secara alami, bernyanyi dan menari sendiri, dan kemunculannya membawa kedamaian bagi dunia.
claims.quote: 背文曰禮，膺文曰仁，腹文曰信。是鳥也，飲食自然，自歌自舞，見則天下安寧

claims.statement: In the Shanhaijing the fenghuang is recorded on Mount Danxue (丹穴之山), which is rich in gold and jade and from which the Dan River flows south into the Bohai Sea.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Shanhaijing, burung fenghuang dicatat berada di gunung Danxue (丹穴之山), yang banyak mengandung emas dan batu giok dan dari sana mengalir Sungai Dan ke arah selatan hingga ke Laut Bohai.
claims.quote: 又東五百里，曰丹穴之山，其上多金玉。丹水出焉，而南流注于渤海

claims.statement: Pangu is a primordial being and creation figure in Chinese mythology and Taoism; according to legend he separated heaven and earth.
claims.statement_id: Pangu adalah makhluk purba dan tokoh penciptaan dalam mitologi Tiongkok dan Taoisme; menurut legenda ia memisahkan langit dan bumi.
claims.quote:
Pangu or Pan Gu (also sometimes spelled Peng Gu and P’an-ku)
(Chinese: 盤古; pinyin: Pángǔ ; PAN-koo) is a primordial being and creation figure in Chinese mythology and in Taoism. According to legend, Pangu separated heaven and earth, and his body later became geographic features such as mountains and flowing water.

claims.statement: Xu Zheng is regarded as an early writer who recorded the Pangu myth, during the Three Kingdoms period.
claims.statement_id: Xu Zheng dianggap sebagai penulis awal yang mencatat mitos Pangu, pada periode Tiga Kerajaan.
claims.quote: The earliest known writer to record the myth of Pangu is believed to have been Xu Zheng during the Three Kingdoms period. However, his name was found in a tomb predating the Three Kingdoms period.

claims.statement: In the cosmic-egg tale, Pangu emerges once yin and yang reach balance.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah telur kosmis, Pangu muncul setelah yin dan yang mencapai keseimbangan.
claims.quote: In the beginning, there was nothing and the universe was in a featureless, formless primordial state. This primordial state coalesced into a cosmic egg over the course of about 18,000 years. Within it, the perfectly opposed principles of yin and yang became balanced and Pangu emerged (or woke up) from the egg. Pangu inside the cosmic egg symbolizes Taiji.

claims.statement: Depictions commonly present Pangu as a hairy giant bearing horns.
claims.statement_id: Pangu lazim digambarkan sebagai raksasa berbulu dengan tanduk di kepala.
claims.quote: Pangu inside the cosmic egg symbolizes Taiji. Pangu is usually depicted as a primitive, hairy giant with horns on his head.

claims.statement: Some versions say Pangu is aided by the Four Auspicious Beasts in creating the world.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian versi menyebut Pangu dibantu Empat Makhluk Bertuah dalam penciptaan dunia.
claims.quote: In some versions of the story, Pangu is aided in this task by the Four Auspicious Beasts (四靈獸). There are many different legends about Pangu's  creation of the world, with some saying that this task took 18,000 years, while others say that he lived for millions of years.

claims.statement: After his death, his breath becomes wind and clouds, his voice becomes thunder, and his eyes become sun and moon.
claims.statement_id: Sesudah kematiannya, napas menjadi angin dan awan, suara menjadi guntur, dan mata menjadi matahari serta bulan.
claims.quote: When Pangu died, his breath became the wind, mist and clouds; his voice, thunder; his left eye, the Sun; his right eye, the Moon; his head, the mountains and extremes of the world; his blood, rivers; his muscles, fertile land; his facial hair, the stars and Milky Way; his fur, bushes and forests; his bones, valuable minerals; his bone marrow, precious jewels; his sweat, rain; and the fle

claims.statement: Werner calls P'an Ku (Pangu) the most conspicuous figure in Chinese cosmogony, the one who chiselled the universe out of Chaos.
claims.statement_id: Werner menyebut P'an Ku (Pangu) sebagai tokoh paling menonjol dalam kosmogoni Tiongkok, yang memahat alam semesta dari Kekacauan.
claims.quote: The most conspicuous figure in Chinese cosmogony is P'an Ku. He it was who chiselled the universe out of Chaos.

claims.statement: According to Werner, 'P'an' means 'the shell of an egg' and 'Ku' 'to secure' or 'solid', referring to P'an Ku being hatched from out of Chaos.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Werner, 'P'an' berarti 'cangkang telur' dan 'Ku' berarti 'mengamankan' atau 'padat', merujuk pada P'an Ku yang menetas dari Kekacauan.
claims.quote: 'P'an' means 'the shell of an egg,' and 'Ku' 'to secure,' 'solid,' referring to P'an Ku being hatched from out of Chaos

claims.statement: According to Werner, P'an Ku is pictured as a dwarfish man clothed in bearskin or leaves, with two horns, holding a hammer in his right hand and a chisel in his left (sometimes reversed).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Werner, P'an Ku digambarkan sebagai pria bertubuh kerdil berpakaian kulit beruang atau daun, bertanduk dua, memegang palu di tangan kanan dan pahat di tangan kiri (kadang terbalik).
claims.quote: P'an Ku is pictured as a man of dwarfish stature clothed in bearskin, or merely in leaves or with an apron of leaves. He has two horns on his head. In his right hand he holds a hammer and in his left a chisel (sometimes these are reversed)

claims.statement: According to Werner, P'an Ku's task occupied eighteen thousand years, during which he formed the sun, moon, stars, heavens and earth, growing six feet taller each day until he died so that his works might live.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Werner, tugas P'an Ku memakan delapan belas ribu tahun; ia membentuk matahari, bulan, bintang, langit, dan bumi sambil bertambah tinggi enam kaki setiap hari, lalu wafat agar karyanya hidup.
claims.quote: His task occupied eighteen thousand years, during which he formed the sun, moon, and stars, the heavens and the earth, himself increasing in stature day by day, being daily six feet taller than the day before, until, his labours ended, he died that his works might live.

claims.statement: In Werner's account, P'an Ku's head became the mountains, his breath the wind and clouds, his voice thunder, his limbs the four quarters of the earth, his blood the rivers, his flesh the soil and his beard the constellations.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penuturan Werner, kepala P'an Ku menjadi gunung, napasnya angin dan awan, suaranya guntur, anggota tubuhnya empat penjuru bumi, darahnya sungai, dagingnya tanah, dan jenggotnya rasi bintang.
claims.quote: His head became the mountains, his breath the wind and clouds, his voice the thunder, his limbs the four quarters of the earth, his blood the rivers, his flesh the soil, his beard the constellations

claims.statement: Werner states that this account of P'an Ku is of Taoist origin, while the Buddhists gave a somewhat different account that is a late adaptation of the Taoist myth.
claims.statement_id: Werner menyatakan bahwa kisah P'an Ku ini berasal dari Tao, sedangkan umat Buddha memberi versi yang agak berbeda sebagai adaptasi belakangan dari mitos Tao.
claims.quote: This account of P'an Ku and his achievements is of Taoist origin. The Buddhists have given a somewhat different account of him, which is a late adaptation from the Taoist myth

claims.statement: According to Werner, other legends say P'an Ku had the head of a dragon and the body of a serpent, and that his breathing caused the wind.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Werner, legenda lain menyebut P'an Ku berkepala naga dan bertubuh ular, dan napasnya menimbulkan angin.
claims.quote: Other legends recount that P'an Ku had the head of a dragon and the body of a serpent; and that by breathing he caused the wind

claims.statement: Mazu is a sea goddess in Chinese folk religion and related religious traditions.
claims.statement_id: Mazu adalah dewi laut dalam agama rakyat Tiongkok dan tradisi keagamaan terkait.
claims.quote: Mazu or Matsu is a sea goddess in Chinese folk religion, Chinese Buddhism, Confucianism, and Taoism. She is also known by several other names and titles. Mazu is the deified form of Lin Moniang (Chinese: 林默娘; pinyin: Lín Mòniáng; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: Lîm Be̍k-niû / Lîm Bia̍k-niû / Lîm Be̍k-niô͘), a shamaness from Fujian who is said to have lived in the late 10th century.

claims.statement: She is understood as the deified Lin Moniang, a woman from Fujian.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipahami sebagai Lin Moniang yang didewakan, seorang perempuan dari Fujian.
claims.quote: Mazu is the deified form of Lin Moniang ... a shamaness from Fujian who is said to have lived in the late 10th century.

claims.statement: Tradition describes miraculous interventions protecting devotees at sea.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi menggambarkannya melindungi pengikut yang berlayar melalui pertolongan ajaib.
claims.quote: Her worship spread throughout China's coastal regions and overseas Chinese communities throughout Southeast Asia, where some Mazu temples are affiliated with famous Taiwanese temples. Traditionally, Mazu was believed to roam the seas, safeguarding her devotees through miraculous interventions.

claims.statement: Her temple celebrations are prominent in Taiwan, notably around Dajia and Beigang.
claims.statement_id: Perayaan kuilnya penting di Taiwan, terutama sekitar Dajia dan Beigang.
claims.quote: Mazu worship is popular in Taiwan because many early Chinese settlers in Taiwan were Hoklo people from Fujian. Her temple festival is a major event in Taiwan, with the largest celebrations occurring in and around her temples at Dajia and Beigang.

claims.statement: During emergencies, invoking Mazu is believed to bring a quicker response than using formal titles.
claims.statement_id: Dalam keadaan darurat, nama Mazu dipercaya mendapat tanggapan lebih cepat daripada gelar resmi.
claims.quote: Although many of Mazu's temples honor her titles Tianhou and Tianfei, it became customary to never pray to her under those names during an emergency since it was believed that, hearing one of her formal titles, Mazu might feel obligated to groom and dress herself as properly befitting her station before receiving the petition.

claims.statement: Legends of Lin Moniang's life were broadly established by the twelfth century.
claims.statement_id: Legenda mengenai kehidupan Lin Moniang sudah terbentuk secara luas pada abad kedua belas.
claims.quote: The legends around Lin Moniang's life were broadly established by the 12th century.

claims.statement: UNESCO describes Mazu as the most influential goddess of the sea in China, at the centre of beliefs and customs including oral traditions, religious ceremonies and folk practices throughout the country's coastal areas.
claims.statement_id: UNESCO menyebut Mazu sebagai dewi laut paling berpengaruh di Tiongkok, yang menjadi pusat berbagai kepercayaan dan adat, termasuk tradisi lisan, upacara keagamaan, dan praktik rakyat di kawasan pesisir negeri itu.
claims.quote: As the most influential goddess of the sea in China, Mazu is at the centre of a host of beliefs and customs, including oral traditions, religious ceremonies and folk practices, throughout the country’s coastal areas.

claims.statement: According to UNESCO, Mazu is believed to have lived in the tenth century on Meizhou Island, dedicated herself to helping her fellow townspeople, and died attempting to rescue shipwreck survivors; local residents built a temple and began to venerate her as a goddess.
claims.statement_id: Menurut deskripsi UNESCO, Mazu dipercaya hidup pada abad kesepuluh di Pulau Meizhou, mengabdikan diri membantu sesama warga, dan wafat saat berusaha menyelamatkan korban kapal karam; warga setempat membangun kuil dan mulai memujanya sebagai dewi.
claims.quote: Mazu is believed to have lived in the tenth century on Meizhou Island, where she dedicated herself to helping her fellow townspeople, and died attempting to rescue the survivors of a shipwreck. Local residents built a temple in her honour and began to venerate her as a goddess.

claims.statement: She is celebrated twice a year in formal temple fairs, when Meizhou residents, farmers and fisherfolk pause their work to sacrifice marine animals, venerate statues of Mazu and enjoy dances and other performances.
claims.statement_id: Ia dirayakan dua kali setahun dalam pekan raya kuil resmi, ketika warga Meizhou, petani, dan nelayan menghentikan pekerjaan sejenak untuk mempersembahkan hewan laut, memuliakan patung Mazu, dan menikmati tarian serta pertunjukan lain.
claims.quote: She is celebrated twice each year in formal temple fairs, when Meizhou residents, farmers and fisherfolk temporarily suspend their work to sacrifice marine animals, venerate statues of Mazu and enjoy a variety of dances and other performances.

claims.statement: Smaller worship ceremonies take place throughout the year in other Mazu temples around the world and in private homes, and may involve floral tributes, candles, incense, firecrackers and evening processions with "Mazu lanterns".
claims.statement_id: Upacara pemujaan yang lebih kecil berlangsung sepanjang tahun di kuil-kuil Mazu lainnya di seluruh dunia dan di rumah pribadi, dapat berupa persembahan bunga, lilin, dupa, petasan, dan arak-arakan malam dengan "lentera Mazu".
claims.quote: Smaller worship ceremonies take place throughout the year in the other 5,000 Mazu temples around the world and in private homes; these may involve floral tributes; candles, incense and firecrackers; and evening processions of residents bearing ‘Mazu lanterns’.

claims.statement: Followers may implore the deity for pregnancy, peace, the solution to a problem or general well-being.
claims.statement_id: Pengikut dapat memohon kepada sang dewa untuk kehamilan, kedamaian, penyelesaian masalah, atau kesejahteraan umum.
claims.quote: Followers may implore the god for pregnancy, peace, the solution to a problem or general well-being.

claims.statement: Mazu belief and customs were inscribed in 2009 on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan dan adat Mazu tercatat pada tahun 2009 dalam Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity milik UNESCO.
claims.quote: Inscribed in 2009 (4.COM) on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity

claims.statement: UNESCO states that belief in and commemoration of Mazu is an important cultural bond that promotes family harmony, social concord and the social identity of coastal Chinese communities and their descendants.
claims.statement_id: UNESCO menyatakan bahwa kepercayaan dan peringatan Mazu menjadi ikatan budaya penting yang mendorong keharmonisan keluarga, kerukunan sosial, dan identitas sosial komunitas pesisir Tiongkok dan keturunan mereka.
claims.quote: Deeply integrated into the lives of coastal Chinese and their descendants, belief in and commemoration of Mazu is an important cultural bond that promotes family harmony, social concord, and the social identity of these communities.

claims.statement: The qilin is a hoofed composite creature in Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Qilin adalah makhluk campuran berkuku dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: is a legendary hooved chimerical creature that appears in Chinese mythology, and is said to appear with the imminent arrival or death of a sage or illustrious ruler. Qilin are a specific type of the lin mythological family of one-horned beasts.

claims.statement: Its appearance is linked to the arrival or death of a sage or distinguished ruler.
claims.statement_id: Kemunculannya dikaitkan dengan kedatangan atau kematian seorang bijak maupun penguasa terkemuka.
claims.quote: is a legendary hooved chimerical creature that appears in Chinese mythology, and is said to appear with the imminent arrival or death of a sage or illustrious ruler. Qilin are a specific type of the lin mythological family of one-horned beasts.

claims.statement: A poem in the Classic of Poetry provides an early mention of the mythical lin.
claims.statement_id: Syair dalam Kitab Nyanyian memuat penyebutan awal lin mitologis.
claims.quote: The earliest mention of the mythical qilin is in the poem 麟之趾; Lín zhī zhǐ; 'Feet of the Lin' included in the Classic of Poetry (11th – 7th c. BCE).

claims.statement: The Spring and Autumn Annals record a lin's capture in Duke Ai of Lu's fourteenth year.
claims.statement_id: Catatan Musim Semi dan Gugur menyebut penangkapan lin pada tahun keempat belas Adipati Ai dari Lu.
claims.quote: Spring and Autumn Annals mentioned that a lin ... was captured in the 14th year of Duke Ai of Lu ... (481 BCE); Zuo Zhuan credited Confucius with identifying the lin as such.

claims.statement: The Shuowen Jiezi assigns qi to the male and lin to the female.
claims.statement_id: Shuowen Jiezi membedakan qi sebagai jantan dan lin sebagai betina.
claims.quote: which carries the same generic meaning as lin alone, is attested in works dated to the Warring States period (475–221 BCE). Qi denotes the male and lin denotes the female according to Shuowen Jiezi.

claims.statement: During the Ming period, qilin imagery was associated with giraffes brought following Zheng He's voyages.
claims.statement_id: Pada zaman Ming, citra qilin dihubungkan dengan jerapah yang dibawa setelah pelayaran Zheng He.
claims.quote: The legendary image of the qilin became associated with the image of the giraffe in the Ming dynasty. The identification of the qilin with giraffes began after Zheng He's 15th-century voyage to East Africa (landing, among other places, Ma-lin (麻林): Malindi (in modern-day Kenya)).

claims.statement: The Kangxi Dictionary, quoting the Shuowen (說文), describes the lin (麟) as a 大麚 with a 麕 body, an ox tail, a wolf forehead and horse hooves, five colours with a yellow belly, and a height recorded as 丈二. The quotation then begins the Yupian (玉篇) entry, which calls it a 仁獸 ("benevolent beast").
claims.statement_id: Kamus Kangxi mengutip Shuowen (說文) tentang lin (麟): disebut 大麚, berbadan 麕, berekor sapi, berdahi serigala, berkuku kuda, berwarna lima dengan perut kuning, dan tingginya tercatat 丈二. Kutipan lalu mengawali Yupian (玉篇) yang menyebutnya 仁獸.
claims.quote: 《說文》大麚也。麕身牛尾，狼額馬蹄，五彩腹下黃，高丈二。《玉篇》仁獸也。

claims.statement: The Kangxi Dictionary quotes the Yupian (玉篇) that the lin is a 仁獸 ("benevolent beast"), then cites the Zhounan poem "Lin zhi zhi" (麟之趾) of the Shi (詩) and the Zhuan (傳) commentary that the lin is trustworthy and responds to ritual propriety.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Kangxi mengutip Yupian (玉篇) bahwa lin adalah 仁獸 ("binatang berbudi"), lalu menyebut syair Zhounan "Lin zhi zhi" (麟之趾) dari kitab Shi (詩) dan komentar Zhuan (傳) bahwa lin bersifat tepercaya dan menanggapi tata upacara.
claims.quote: 《玉篇》仁獸也。《詩·周南》麟之趾。《傳》麟信而應禮，以足至者也。

claims.statement: The Kangxi Dictionary quotes the Da Dai Liji (大戴禮) that among the 三百六十 (three hundred and sixty) furred creatures the lin is the chief (長), and the Liji chapter Liyun (禮運) that when the lin is kept as a domestic animal (以爲畜), 獸不狘 ("the beasts do not 狘").
claims.statement_id: Kamus Kangxi mengutip Da Dai Liji (大戴禮) bahwa di antara 三百六十 jenis makhluk berbulu, lin menjadi pemimpinnya (長), dan Liji bab Liyun (禮運) bahwa bila lin dipelihara (以爲畜), maka 獸不狘.
claims.quote: 《大戴禮》毛蟲三百六十，麟爲之長。《禮·禮運》麟以爲畜，故獸不狘。

claims.statement: The Kangxi Dictionary quotes the Shuowen (說文) that the qi (麒) is a 仁獸 ("benevolent beast") with a 麕 body, an ox tail and one horn (一角); Zhang Yi (張揖) says the qi is the male (牡) and the lin the female (牝); Guo Pu (郭璞) says the qi resembles the lin but has no horn (無角).
claims.statement_id: Kamus Kangxi mengutip Shuowen (說文) bahwa qi (麒) adalah 仁獸 berbadan 麕, berekor sapi, dan bertanduk satu (一角); Zhang Yi (張揖) menyebut qi jantan (牡) dan lin betina (牝); Guo Pu (郭璞) menyatakan qi mirip lin tetapi tanpa tanduk (無角).
claims.quote: 《說文》仁獸也。麕身牛尾，一角。張揖云：牡曰麒，牝曰麟。郭璞曰：麒似麟而無角。

claims.statement: The Liji chapter Liyun (禮運) asks what the 四靈 ("four spirits") are and answers: the lin (麟), the feng bird (鳳), the tortoise (龜) and the dragon (龍). The quotation continues that when the dragon is kept as a domestic animal (以爲畜), 魚鮪不淰.
claims.statement_id: Liji bab Liyun (禮運) bertanya apa itu 四靈 ("empat makhluk gaib") dan menjawab: lin (麟), burung feng (鳳), kura-kura (龜), dan naga (龍). Kutipan lanjut menyebut bahwa bila naga dipelihara (以爲畜), 魚鮪不淰.
claims.quote: 何謂四靈？麟、鳳、龜、龍，謂之四靈。故龍以爲畜，故魚鮪不淰；

claims.statement: The Zuo Zhuan (春秋左氏傳) records that in the spring of the fourteenth year, during a hunt in the west at Daye (大野), Chu Shang (鉏商) of the Shusun clan (叔孫氏) caught a lin (獲麟); it was taken as inauspicious (不祥) and given to the forester (虞人), then Zhongni (仲尼) examined it and said "麟也" ("it is a lin"), after which it was taken.
claims.statement_id: Zuo Zhuan (春秋左氏傳) mencatat bahwa pada musim semi tahun keempat belas, dalam perburuan di Daye (大野) di barat, Chu Shang (鉏商) dari keluarga Shusun (叔孫氏) menangkap seekor lin (獲麟); hewan itu dianggap pertanda buruk (不祥) dan diberikan kepada penjaga hutan (虞人), lalu Zhongni (仲尼) memeriksanya dan berkata "麟也" ("itu lin"), sesudahnya hewan itu diambil.
claims.quote: 十四年春．西狩于大野．叔孫氏之車子鉏商獲麟．以為不祥．以賜虞人．仲尼觀之．曰．麟也．然後取之．

claims.statement: Zhuque, the Vermilion Bird, belongs to the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations.
claims.statement_id: Zhuque atau Burung Merah adalah salah satu Empat Lambang rasi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: The Vermilion Bird (Chinese: 朱雀; pinyin: Zhūquè) is one of the Four Symbols of the Chinese constellations. According to Wu Xing, the Taoist five elemental system, it represents the Fire element, the direction south, and the season of summer correspondingly. Thus it is sometimes called the Vermilion Bird of the South (Chinese: 南方朱雀; pinyin: Nánfāng Zhūquè).

claims.statement: In the five-phase system, it corresponds to fire, south, and summer.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sistem lima unsur, ia mewakili api, selatan, dan musim panas.
claims.quote: The Vermilion Bird (Chinese: 朱雀; pinyin: Zhūquè) is one of the Four Symbols of the Chinese constellations. According to Wu Xing, the Taoist five elemental system, it represents the Fire element, the direction south, and the season of summer correspondingly. Thus it is sometimes called the Vermilion Bird of the South (Chinese: 南方朱雀; pinyin: Nánfāng Zhūquè).

claims.statement: The Vermilion Bird is a constellation spirit distinct from fenghuang.
claims.statement_id: Burung Merah merupakan roh rasi yang berbeda dari fenghuang.
claims.quote: It is often mistaken for the fenghuang due to similarities in appearance, but the two are different creatures. The fenghuang is a legendary ruler of birds who is associated with the Chinese Empress in the same way the dragon is associated with the Emperor, while the Vermilion Bird is a mythological spirit creature of the Chinese constellations.

claims.statement: Seven lunar mansions are grouped within its constellation region.
claims.statement_id: Tujuh kedudukan bulan dikelompokkan dalam wilayah rasi Burung Merah.
claims.quote: As with the other three Symbols, there are seven astrological "Mansions" (positions of the Moon) within the Vermilion Bird. The names and determinative stars are:

claims.statement: In the Liji (Quli shang), on the march the Vermilion Bird (朱鳥) is in front, Xuanwu behind, the Azure Dragon (青龍) on the left and the White Tiger (白虎) on the right.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Liji (Quli shang), pada saat berjalan, Zhuniao (朱鳥) berada di depan, Xuanwu di belakang, Naga Biru (青龍) di kiri, dan Harimau Putih (白虎) di kanan.
claims.quote: 前朱鳥 ... 而後玄武，左青龍而右白虎，招摇在上，急繕其怒。

claims.statement: In the Huainanzi (Tianwen xun), the south is fire, with the Flame Emperor (炎帝) as its emperor, governing summer, and its beast is the Zhuniao (朱鳥, Vermilion Bird).
claims.statement_id: Dalam Huainanzi (Tianwen xun), selatan adalah api dengan Kaisar Yan sebagai penguasanya, memerintah musim panas, dan binatangnya adalah Zhuniao (朱鳥).
claims.quote: 南方，火也，其帝炎帝，其佐朱明，執衡而治夏。其神為熒惑，其獸朱鳥，其音徵，其日丙丁。

claims.statement: In the Huainanzi (Tianwen xun), Taiwei is said to govern Zhuque (朱雀).
claims.statement_id: Dalam Huainanzi (Tianwen xun), Taiwei disebut menguasai Zhuque (朱雀).
claims.quote: 咸池者，水魚之囿也。天阿者，群神之闕也。四宮者，所以為司賞罰。太微者主朱雀，紫宮執斗而左旋，日行一度，以周於天。

claims.statement: In the Zhengyi commentary to the Shiji (Tianguan shu), the eight stars of Liu (柳) are called the beak (咮) of the Zhuniao (朱鳥) and are linked to the heavenly cook in charge of food.
claims.statement_id: Dalam komentar Zhengyi pada Shiji (Tianguan shu), delapan bintang Liu (柳) disebut sebagai paruh (咮) Zhuniao (朱鳥) dan dikaitkan dengan juru masak surga yang mengurusi makanan.
claims.quote: 柳八星，星七星，張六星，爲鶉火，於辰在午，皆周之分野。柳爲朱鳥咮，天之廚宰，主尚食，和滋味。

claims.statement: The Suoyin commentary to the Shiji (Tianguan shu) quotes the Wenyaogou: the Red Emperor of the Southern Palace, whose essence is the Zhuniao (朱鳥).
claims.statement_id: Komentar Suoyin pada Shiji (Tianguan shu) mengutip Wenyaogou: Kaisar Merah dari Istana Selatan, esensinya adalah Zhuniao (朱鳥).
claims.quote: 孟康曰：「軒轅爲權，太微爲衡。」【索隱】案：文耀鈎云「南宮赤帝，其精爲朱鳥」。

claims.statement: Black Tortoise, or Xuanwu, is a Chinese constellation symbol showing a turtle intertwined with a snake.
claims.statement_id: Black Tortoise atau Xuanwu adalah lambang rasi Tiongkok berupa kura-kura yang dililit ular.
claims.quote: The Black Turtle-Snake (Chinese: 玄武; pinyin: Xuánwǔ) is one of the Four Symbols of the Chinese constellations. It is usually depicted as a tortoise or turtle, intertwined with a snake.

claims.statement: Xu Shen's explanation links wu to the word for knight in the Jianghuai dialect.
claims.statement_id: Penjelasan Xu Shen mengaitkan kata wu dengan kesatria dalam dialek Jianghuai.
claims.quote: According to Eastern Han philologist Xu Shen, the character wu (武) meant "knight" (士; shì ) in the Jianghuai dialect.  So the English translation Black ~ Dark ~ Mysterious Warrior is a more faithful translation.

claims.statement: Xuanwu is associated with the northern direction.
claims.statement_id: Xuanwu dikaitkan dengan arah utara.
claims.quote: It represents the north, thus it is sometimes called Black Warrior of the North (北方玄武; Běifāng Xuánwǔ).

claims.statement: The winter association draws on the hibernation of turtles and snakes.
claims.statement_id: Kura-kura dan ular yang berhibernasi mendasari hubungannya dengan musim dingin.
claims.quote: While neither character xuan (玄) or wu (武) literally means turtle, tortoise or snake, tortoises and snakes are known to hibernate during winter, so xuanwu (玄武) as a whole represents the season of winter.

claims.statement: In Japan, Genbu is believed to guard Kyoto's northern side.
claims.statement_id: Di Jepang, Genbu dipercaya menjaga sisi utara Kyoto.
claims.quote: In Japan, the characters xuanwu (玄武) are pronounced as Genbu. It is said to protect Kyoto on the north side, being one of the four guardian spirits that protect the city. It is represented by the Kenkun Shrine, which is located on top of Mount Funaoka in Kyoto.

claims.statement: The Liji (Quli) text says that on the march Xuanwu (玄武) is behind, the Azure Dragon (青龍) on the left and the White Tiger (白虎) on the right, with the Zhaoyao (招摇) banner above.
claims.statement_id: Teks Liji (Quli) menyebut bahwa dalam perjalanan, Xuanwu (玄武) berada di belakang, Naga Biru-Hijau (青龍) di kiri, dan Harimau Putih (白虎) di kanan, dengan panji Zhaoyao (招摇) di atas.
claims.quote: 鳥一作「雀」而後玄武，左青龍而右白虎，招摇在上，急繕其怒。進退有度，左右有局，各司其局。

claims.statement: In the poem Yuan You (Chu Ci), the traveller summons Xuanwu (玄武) to hasten after him, then has Wenchang (文昌) manage the journey and choose the gods to accompany his chariot.
claims.statement_id: Dalam syair Yuan You (Chu Ci), tokoh yang bepergian memanggil Xuanwu (玄武) untuk bergegas mengikutinya, lalu Wenchang (文昌) diminta mengurus perjalanan dan memilih para dewa untuk mengiringi keretanya.
claims.quote: 旹曖曃其曭莽兮，召玄武而奔屬。後文昌使掌行兮，選署衆神以並轂。

claims.statement: In ancient China, the tortoise (or turtle) and the serpent were thought to be spiritual creatures symbolizing longevity.
claims.statement_id: Di Tiongkok kuno, kura-kura dan ular dianggap makhluk spiritual yang melambangkan umur panjang.
claims.quote: In ancient China, the tortoise (or turtle) and the serpent were thought to be spiritual creatures symbolizing longevity.

claims.statement: In the classic novel Journey to the West, Xuanwu is a king of the north with two generals under him, a "Tortoise General" and a "Snake General".
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel klasik Journey to the West, Xuanwu adalah raja utara yang memiliki dua jenderal, "Jenderal Kura-kura" dan "Jenderal Ular".
claims.quote: In the classic novel Journey to the West, Xuanwu was a king of the north who had two generals serving under him, a "Tortoise General" and a "Snake General".

claims.statement: White Tiger belongs to the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations.
claims.statement_id: White Tiger adalah Harimau Putih dalam Empat Lambang rasi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: is one of the Four Symbols of the Chinese constellations. It is sometimes called the White Tiger of the West

claims.statement: The White Tiger corresponds to west and autumn.
claims.statement_id: Harimau Putih berhubungan dengan arah barat dan musim gugur.
claims.quote: It represents the west in terms of direction and the autumn season.

claims.statement: Its names in neighboring traditions include Japanese Byakko and Korean Baekho.
claims.statement_id: Nama lintas bahasanya meliputi Byakko di Jepang dan Baekho di Korea.
claims.quote: It is known as Byakko in Japanese, Baekho in Korean, and Bạch Hổ in Vietnamese.

claims.statement: The White Tiger's constellation region contains seven lunar mansions.
claims.statement_id: Wilayah rasi Harimau Putih mencakup tujuh kedudukan bulan.
claims.quote: As with the other three Symbols, there are seven astrological "Mansions" (positions of the Moon) within the White Tiger. The names and determinative stars are:

claims.statement: The Huainanzi chapter Tianwen xun (天文訓) says the west is metal (金), its emperor is Shaohao (少昊) and its assistant Rushou (蓐收), who holds the square and governs autumn (治秋); its spirit is Taibai (太白) and its beast (獸) is the White Tiger (白虎).
claims.statement_id: Huainanzi bab Tianwen xun (天文訓) menyebut bahwa arah barat adalah logam (金), kaisarnya Shaohao (少昊), pembantunya Rushou (蓐收) yang memegang penyiku dan mengatur musim gugur (治秋); rohnya adalah Taibai (太白) dan binatangnya (獸) adalah Harimau Putih (白虎).
claims.quote: 西方，金也，其帝少昊，其佐蓐收，執矩而治秋。其神為太白，其獸白虎，其音商，其日庚辛。

claims.statement: The Liji chapter Quli shang (曲禮上) puts the Azure Dragon (青龍) on the left and the White Tiger (白虎) on the right, with 招摇 (Zhaoyao) above; advance and retreat follow rules and each part keeps its own post.
claims.statement_id: Liji bab Quli shang (曲禮上) menempatkan Naga Biru (青龍) di sisi kiri dan Harimau Putih (白虎) di sisi kanan, dengan 招摇 (Zhaoyao) di atas; gerak maju-mundur berpedoman pada aturan dan tiap bagian memegang tugas masing-masing.
claims.quote: 左青龍而右白虎，招摇在上，急繕其怒。進退有度，左右有局，各司其局。

claims.statement: Werner writes that the functions discharged by Heng and Ha at the gates of Buddhist temples are discharged in Taoist temples by Blue Dragon and White Tiger.
claims.statement_id: Werner menulis bahwa tugas yang dijalankan Heng dan Ha di gerbang kuil Buddha dijalankan di kuil Tao oleh Blue Dragon (Naga Biru) dan White Tiger (Harimau Putih).
claims.quote: The functions discharged by Heng and Ha at the gates of Buddhist temples are in Taoist temples discharged by Blue Dragon and White Tiger.

claims.statement: Werner states that the Spirit of the White Tiger Star is Yin Ch'eng-hsiu, whose father Yin P'o-pai, a high courtier of the tyrant Chou Wang, was sent to negotiate peace with Chiang Tzu-ya but was seized and put to death by Marquis Chiang Wen-huan.
claims.statement_id: Werner menyebut bahwa Roh Bintang Harimau Putih adalah Yin Ch'eng-hsiu, putra Yin P'o-pai, pejabat tinggi istana tiran Chou Wang yang dikirim berunding damai dengan Chiang Tzu-ya tetapi ditangkap dan dihukum mati oleh Marquis Chiang Wen-huan.
claims.quote: The Spirit of the White Tiger Star is Yin Ch'eng-hsiu. His father, Yin P'o-pai, a high courtier of the tyrant Chou Wang, was sent to negotiate peace with Chiang Tzu-ya, but was seized and put to death by Marquis Chiang Wen-huan.

claims.statement: According to Werner, the son, trying to avenge his father's murder, was pierced by a spear and his head was cut off and carried in triumph to Chiang Tzu-ya; as compensation he was, though somewhat tardily, canonized as the Spirit of the White Tiger Star.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Werner, putra itu berusaha membalas kematian ayahnya tetapi ditombak dan kepalanya dipenggal serta dibawa dengan kemenangan kepada Chiang Tzu-ya; sebagai ganti rugi ia, meski agak terlambat, diangkat sebagai Roh Bintang Harimau Putih.
claims.quote: His son, attempting to avenge his father's murder, was pierced by a spear, and his head was cut off and carried in triumph to Chiang Tzu-ya. As compensation he was, though somewhat tardily, canonized as the Spirit of the White Tiger Star.

claims.statement: The Azure Dragon is a Chinese dragon counted among the Four Symbols of the constellations.
claims.statement_id: Azure Dragon adalah naga Tiongkok yang termasuk Empat Lambang rasi.
claims.quote: The Azure Dragon (simplified Chinese: 青龙; traditional Chinese: 青龍; pinyin: Qīnglóng) is one of the Dragon Gods who represent the mounts or chthonic forces of the Five Regions' Highest Deities (五方上帝; Wǔfāng Shàngdì). It is also one of the Four Symbols of the Chinese constellations, which are the astral representations of the Wufang Shangdi.

claims.statement: It corresponds to the eastern direction and spring.
claims.statement_id: Ia mewakili timur dan musim semi.
claims.quote: The Azure Dragon represents the east and the spring season.

claims.statement: This dragon is also known as Seiryū in Japanese, Cheongryong in Korean and Thanh Long in Vietnamese.
claims.statement_id: Naga ini dikenal sebagai Seiryū dalam bahasa Jepang, Cheongryong dalam bahasa Korea, dan Thanh Long dalam bahasa Vietnam.
claims.quote: This dragon is also known as Seiryū in Japanese, Cheongryong in Korean and Thanh Long in Vietnamese.

claims.statement: Its constellation region comprises seven lunar mansions.
claims.statement_id: Wilayah rasi naga ini mencakup tujuh kedudukan bulan.
claims.quote: As with the other three Symbols, there are seven astrological "Mansions" (positions of the Moon) within the Azure Dragon. The names and determinative stars are:

claims.statement: The Azure Dragon also appears as a door deity in Taoist temples.
claims.statement_id: Azure Dragon juga muncul sebagai dewa pintu di kuil Tao.
claims.quote: The Azure Dragon appears as a door god at Taoist temples. He was represented on the tomb of Wang Hui (stone coffin, east side) at Xikang in Lushan. A rubbing of this was collected by David Crockett Graham and is in the Field Museum of Natural History. The dragon featured on the Chinese national flag in 1862–1912, and on the Twelve Symbols national emblem from 1913 to 1928.

claims.statement: Goguryeo tomb murals at Uhyon-ni depict this dragon with the other symbols.
claims.statement_id: Lukisan makam Goguryeo di Uhyon-ni menampilkan naga ini bersama lambang lainnya.
claims.quote: In Korea, the murals of the Goguryeo tombs found at Uhyon-ni in South Pyongan province features the Azure Dragon and the other mythological creatures of the four symbols.

claims.statement: De Visser, citing De Groot, writes that blue is chosen in China because it is the colour of the East, from where the rain must come; this quarter is represented by the Azure Dragon, the highest in rank among all the dragons.
claims.statement_id: De Visser, mengutip De Groot, menulis bahwa warna biru dipilih di Tiongkok karena merupakan warna timur, asal hujan; penjuru ini diwakili Naga Biru-Hijau, yang tertinggi dalam peringkat di antara semua naga.
claims.quote: According to Dr Groot, the colour blue is chosen in China because this is the colour of the East, from where the rain must come; this quarter is represented by the Azure Dragon, the highest in rank among all the dragons.

claims.statement: De Visser writes that the azure dragon is the symbol of Spring.
claims.statement_id: De Visser menulis bahwa naga biru-hijau adalah lambang musim semi.
claims.quote: The azure dragon is, as we stated above, the symbol of Spring, the season when

claims.statement: De Visser records that on the night of Confucius' birth (551 BC) two azure dragons descended from the sky.
claims.statement_id: De Visser mencatat bahwa pada malam kelahiran Konfusius (551 SM) dua naga biru-hijau turun dari langit.
claims.quote: In the night of Confucius’ birth (B.C. 551) two azure dragons descended from the sky

claims.statement: According to De Visser, the appearance of yellow or azure dragons was nearly always considered a very good omen.
claims.statement_id: Menurut De Visser, kemunculan naga kuning atau biru-hijau hampir selalu dianggap pertanda yang sangat baik.
claims.quote: The appearance of yellow or azure dragons ... was nearly always considered to be a very good omen.

claims.statement: In Japan, the Azure Dragon is one of the four guardian spirits of cities and is believed to protect the city of Kyoto on the east.
claims.statement_id: Di Jepang, Naga Biru-Hijau adalah satu dari empat roh penjaga kota dan dipercaya melindungi sisi timur Kyoto.
claims.quote: In Japan, the Azure Dragon is one of the four guardian spirits of cities and is believed to protect the city of Kyoto on the east.

claims.statement: The Azure Dragon is associated with the East Sea Dragon King Ao Guang, who is the Dragon King Sagara in Buddhist literature.
claims.statement_id: Naga Biru-Hijau dikaitkan dengan Raja Naga Laut Timur Ao Guang, yang dalam sastra Buddha adalah Raja Naga Sagara.
claims.quote: The Azure Dragon is associated with the East Sea Dragon King Ao Guang, who is the Dragon King Sagara in Buddhist literature.

claims.statement: The Liji (Quli) text says that on the march Xuanwu (玄武) is behind, the Azure Dragon (青龍) on the left and the White Tiger (白虎) on the right, with the Zhaoyao (招摇) banner above.
claims.statement_id: Teks Liji (Quli) menyebut bahwa dalam perjalanan, Xuanwu (玄武) berada di belakang, Naga Biru-Hijau (青龍) di kiri, dan Harimau Putih (白虎) di kanan, dengan panji Zhaoyao (招摇) di atas.
claims.quote: 鳥一作「雀」而後玄武，左青龍而右白虎，招摇在上，急繕其怒。進退有度，左右有局，各司其局。

claims.statement: The dragon is also sometimes called the Blue-Green Dragon, Green Dragon, or Blue Dragon.
claims.statement_id: Naga ini kadang disebut juga Naga Biru-Hijau, Naga Hijau, atau Naga Biru.
claims.quote: It is also sometimes referred to as the Blue-Green Dragon, Green Dragon, or the Blue Dragon

claims.statement: Tengri names a principal deity in early Turkic and Mongol traditions.
claims.statement_id: Tengri adalah sebutan dewa utama dalam tradisi Turk dan Mongol awal.
claims.quote: Ini juga merupakan salah satu istilah yang digunakan untuk dewa utama masyarakat Turki dan Mongol awal.

claims.statement: The Tengri concept includes the clear blue sky and a deity of fate.
claims.statement_id: Konsep Tengri mencakup langit biru yang jernih dan peran dewa nasib.
claims.quote: 「テングリ」は中国史における「天」概念と非常に類似しており、天上世界を指すとともに運命神であることも共通している。ただし中国史において天の人格神である天帝が北極星と同一視されているのに対し、テングリは澄みきった青空のことであると考えられており、その点で相違する。「テングリ」崇拝は匈奴の時代から確認されている。

claims.statement: In Mongol creation mythology, Tengri Khairkhan appears as the creator of the earth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos penciptaan Mongol, Tengri Khairkhan muncul sebagai pencipta bumi.
claims.quote: また、人格神としての「テングリ」はモンゴルの宇宙創造神話において「テングリ・ハイラハン」という地上を作った創造神として現れ、これも中国には見られない。ブリヤート族の神話では「西の善きテングリ」「東の悪しきテングリ」という表現が見られ、この二元性は祆教の影響によるものとも考えられている。また、このことからテングリは必ずしも唯一的な存在ではないことも看取され、これも天とは相違する。テングリは男性神であり、女性神である大地に対応する。

claims.statement: The Han shu (漢書) records that the Xiongnu call heaven 撐犁 (chengli) and a son 孤塗 (gutu); their state called its ruler 撐犁孤塗單于, and the word 單于 is explained as meaning "vast and great", said to express resemblance to heaven.
claims.statement_id: Han shu (漢書) mencatat bahwa orang Xiongnu menyebut langit 撐犁 (chengli) dan anak 孤塗 (gutu); negeri itu menyebut pemimpinnya 撐犁孤塗單于, dan kata 單于 dijelaskan sebagai "luas besar" yang melambangkan keserupaan dengan langit.
claims.quote: 單于姓攣鞮氏，其國稱之曰「撐犁孤塗單于」。匈奴謂天為「撐犁」，謂子為「孤塗」，單于者，廣大之貌也，言其象天單于然也。

claims.statement: According to this article, the oldest form of the name is recorded in Chinese annals from the 4th century BC describing Xiongnu beliefs, in the form 撑犁 (Cheng-li), hypothesized to be a Chinese transcription of Tängri.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, bentuk tertua nama itu tercatat dalam arsip Tiongkok sejak abad ke-4 SM dalam uraian kepercayaan Xiongnu, berbentuk 撑犁 (Cheng-li), yang diduga merupakan transkripsi Tiongkok dari Tängri.
claims.quote: The oldest form of the name is recorded in Chinese annals from the 4th century BC, describing the beliefs of the Xiongnu. It takes the form 撑犁/Cheng-li, which is hypothesized to be a Chinese transcription of Tängri.

claims.statement: The article states that the word tengri is generally assumed to have originally meant "sky".
claims.statement_id: Artikel ini menyatakan bahwa kata tengri umumnya diasumsikan semula berarti "langit".
claims.quote: It is generally assumed the term tengri originally meant "sky".

claims.statement: According to this article, Tengri was the national god of the Göktürks, described as the "god of the Turks" (Türük Tängrisi), and the Göktürk khans based their power on a mandate from Tengri.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, Tengri adalah dewa nasional bangsa Göktürk, disebut "dewa bangsa Turk" (Türük Tängrisi), dan para khan Göktürk mendasarkan kekuasaan mereka pada mandat dari Tengri.
claims.quote: Tengri was the national god of the Göktürks, described as the "god of the Turks" (Türük Tängrisi). The Göktürk khans based their power on a mandate from Tengri.

claims.statement: The article quotes the inscription dedicated to Kul Tigin (in the translation provided by the Language Committee of the Republic of Kazakhstan): "When the blue sky [Tengri] above and the brown earth below were created, between them a human being was created."
claims.statement_id: Artikel ini mengutip prasasti untuk Kul Tigin (terjemahan Komite Bahasa Kazakhstan): "Ketika langit biru [Tengri] di atas dan bumi cokelat di bawah diciptakan, di antara keduanya manusia diciptakan."
claims.quote: The inscription dedicated to Kul Tigin includes the passages (in the translation provided by the Language Committee of Ministry of Culture and Information of the Republic of Kazakhstan): "When the blue sky [Tengri] above and the brown earth below were created, between them a human being was created.

claims.statement: The article quotes the Orkhon inscriptions, where Bilge Kaghan calls himself "Tengri-like and Tengri-born Turk Bilge Kaghan" who succeeded to the throne at that time.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ini mengutip prasasti Orkhon, tempat Bilge Kagan menyebut dirinya "Turk Bilge Kagan yang seperti Tengri dan lahir dari Tengri" yang naik takhta pada masa itu.
claims.quote: Orkhon inscriptions in the following way: "I, Tengri-like and Tengri-born Turk Bilge Kaghan, succeeded to the throne at this time"

claims.statement: The Dragon King is a water and weather deity in Asian traditions, including Chinese folk religion.
claims.statement_id: Dragon King adalah dewa air dan cuaca yang dikenal dalam tradisi Asia, termasuk agama rakyat Tiongkok.
claims.quote: The Dragon King, also known as the Dragon God, is a celestial creature, water and weather god in Asian mythology. They can be found in various cultural and religious symbolic materials all around Asia, specifically in South, Southeast Asia and distinctly in East Asian cultures (Chinese folk-religion).

claims.statement: Belief attributes rainfall and dominion over seas, rivers, and other waters to him.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipercaya mengatur hujan serta menguasai laut, sungai, dan badan air lainnya.
claims.quote: He can manipulate and control the weather, move seasons and bring rainfall with his divine power at his own will, thus, he is regarded as the dispenser of rain, divine ruler of the Seas, rivers and water bodies,  commanding over all bodies of water.  He is the collective personification of the ancient concept of the lóng in Chinese culture and Nāgarāja in Indian culture.

claims.statement: Accounts describe his underwater palace and royal court system.
claims.statement_id: Kisah menggambarkan istana bawah air dan sistem istana kerajaan miliknya.
claims.quote: It is described that they have their own under-water palace and a royal court system of their own.

claims.statement: The tradition also recognizes the Dragon Kings of the Four Seas.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi juga mengenal Raja Naga Empat Laut.
claims.quote: There are also the cosmological "Dragon Kings of the Four Seas" (四海龍王; Sihai Longwang).

claims.statement: The dragon deity may also serve as a territorial protector.
claims.statement_id: Dewa naga dapat berperan sebagai pelindung wilayah.
claims.quote: Besides being a water deity, the Dragon God frequently also serves as a territorial tutelary deity, similarly to Tudigong "Lord of the Earth" and Houtu "Queen of the Earth".

claims.statement: Farming villages formerly held rites at dragon-king shrines to seek rain.
claims.statement_id: Desa pertanian dahulu mengadakan upacara di kuil raja naga untuk meminta hujan.
claims.quote: In the past, there used to be Dragon King miao shrines all over China, for the folk to engage in the worship of dragon kings, villages in farm countries would conduct rites dedicated to the Dragon Kings seeking rain.

claims.statement: According to Werner, the Sea-dragon Kings live in splendid palaces in the depths of the sea and feed on pearls and opals. There are five: the chief in the centre and four others in the north, west, south, and east.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Werner, Raja Naga Laut tinggal di istana megah di dasar laut dan memakan mutiara dan opal. Mereka berjumlah lima: satu yang utama di tengah, empat lainnya di utara, barat, selatan, dan timur.
claims.quote: The Sea-dragon Kings live in gorgeous palaces in the depths of the sea, where they feed on pearls and opals. There are five of these divinities, the chief being in the centre, and the other four occupying the north, the west, the south, and the east.

claims.statement: According to Werner, the five Sea-dragon Kings are all immortal and know each other's thoughts, plans, and wishes without communicating.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Werner, kelima Raja Naga Laut itu abadi dan saling mengetahui pikiran, rencana, dan keinginan tanpa perlu berkomunikasi.
claims.quote: The five Sea-dragon Kings are all immortal. They know each other's thoughts, plans, and wishes without intercommunication.

claims.statement: According to Werner, like the other gods the Sea-dragon Kings go up once a year to the Heavens to make an annual report to the Supreme Ruler, in the third month.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Werner, seperti dewa-dewa lain, para Raja Naga Laut naik setahun sekali ke Surga untuk membuat laporan tahunan kepada Penguasa Tertinggi, yaitu pada bulan ketiga.
claims.quote: Like all the other gods they go once a year to the superior Heavens, to make an annual report to the Supreme Ruler; but they go in the third month

claims.statement: According to Werner, in the spirit-world a Ministry of Waters has a Department of Salt Waters presided over by four Dragon-kings, those of the East, South, West, and North.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Werner, di dunia roh ada Kementerian Perairan; Departemen Air Asin dipimpin empat Raja Naga dari Timur, Selatan, Barat, dan Utara.
claims.quote: Its main divisions are the Department of Salt Waters, presided over by four Dragon-kings--those of the East, South, West, and North--and the Department of Sweet Waters

claims.statement: Druk is the thunder dragon of Tibetan and Bhutanese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Druk adalah naga guntur dalam mitologi Tibet dan Bhutan.
claims.quote: The Druk (Standard Tibetan: འབྲུག, Dzongkha: འབྲུག་) is the "thunder dragon" of Tibetan and Bhutanese mythology and a Bhutanese national symbol. A druk appears on the flag of Bhutan, holding jewels to represent wealth. In Dzongkha, Bhutan is called Druk Yul "Land of Druk", and Bhutanese leaders are called Druk Gyalpo, "Thunder Dragon Kings".

claims.statement: On Bhutan's flag, Druk holds jewels symbolizing wealth.
claims.statement_id: Pada bendera Bhutan, Druk memegang permata yang melambangkan kekayaan.
claims.quote: The Druk (Standard Tibetan: འབྲུག, Dzongkha: འབྲུག་) is the "thunder dragon" of Tibetan and Bhutanese mythology and a Bhutanese national symbol. A druk appears on the flag of Bhutan, holding jewels to represent wealth. In Dzongkha, Bhutan is called Druk Yul "Land of Druk", and Bhutanese leaders are called Druk Gyalpo, "Thunder Dragon Kings".

claims.statement: Bhutan's name Druk Yul means Land of Druk.
claims.statement_id: Nama Druk Yul untuk Bhutan berarti Tanah Druk.
claims.quote: The Druk (Standard Tibetan: འབྲུག, Dzongkha: འབྲུག་) is the "thunder dragon" of Tibetan and Bhutanese mythology and a Bhutanese national symbol. A druk appears on the flag of Bhutan, holding jewels to represent wealth. In Dzongkha, Bhutan is called Druk Yul "Land of Druk", and Bhutanese leaders are called Druk Gyalpo, "Thunder Dragon Kings".

claims.statement: The Drukpa lineage originating in Tibet adopted Druk as its emblem.
claims.statement_id: Aliran Drukpa yang berasal dari Tibet mengadopsi Druk sebagai lambang.
claims.quote: The druk (also known as a "duk" or "dug") was adopted as an emblem by the Drukpa Lineage, which originated in Tibet and spread to Bhutan.  According to traditional accounts, when the sect's founder, Tsangpa Gyare, 1st Gyalwang Drukpa, began to build Ralung Monastery, there was a violent storm.  Thunder, or the "Cloud-Voice", is seen as the roar of the dragon.

claims.statement: The Ralung foundation story connects a storm and thunder with a dragon's roar.
claims.statement_id: Kisah pendirian Ralung mengaitkan badai dan guntur dengan raungan naga.
claims.quote: The druk (also known as a "duk" or "dug") was adopted as an emblem by the Drukpa Lineage, which originated in Tibet and spread to Bhutan.  According to traditional accounts, when the sect's founder, Tsangpa Gyare, 1st Gyalwang Drukpa, began to build Ralung Monastery, there was a violent storm.  Thunder, or the "Cloud-Voice", is seen as the roar of the dragon.

claims.statement: According to this journal article, Tsangpa Gyare or Yeshe Dorji (1161–1211) was the main disciple of Lingchen Repa Pema Dorji and the founder of "Bhutan's Dragon Tradition", the Drukpa Kagyu Lineage.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel jurnal ini, Tsangpa Gyare atau Yeshe Dorji (1161–1211) adalah murid utama Lingchen Repa Pema Dorji dan pendiri "Tradisi Naga Bhutan", yaitu Garis Silsilah Drukpa Kagyu.
claims.quote: Tsangpa Gyare or Yeshe Dorji (1161–1211) was the main disciple of Lingchen Repa Pema Dorji and the founder of the Bhutan’s Dragon Tradition – Drukpa Kagyu Lineage

claims.statement: The article states that Druk is highly regarded by the lineage of Drukpa Tsangpa Gyare/Yeshe Dorji, and became the name of the country after the arrival of Shabdrung Ngawang Namgyel in 1616 and the first monastic establishment in 1621 at Chagri Dorji Dhen.
claims.statement_id: Artikel itu menyatakan bahwa Druk sangat dihormati oleh garis silsilah Drukpa Tsangpa Gyare/Yeshe Dorji, dan menjadi nama negeri setelah kedatangan Shabdrung Ngawang Namgyel pada 1616 serta berdirinya biara pertama pada 1621 di Chagri Dorji Dhen.

claims.statement: According to the article, the country of Bhutan is called "Druk", the land "Drukyul", and the people "Drukpa".
