claims.quote: Several accounts describe its appearance, with some claiming that it resembles a flat-faced lion with the body of a dog and prominent incisors.

claims.statement: A legend explains red lanterns as an attempt to avert Nian's attacks.
claims.statement_id: Legenda menjelaskan pemasangan lentera merah sebagai upaya menghindari serangan Nian.
claims.quote: Some local legends attribute the Chinese lion dance (舞獅) to the nian. The tradition has its origins in a story of a nian's attack on a village. After the attack, the villagers discussed how to make the nian leave them in peace. Since it was discovered that the beast was afraid of the color red, people put red lanterns and spring scrolls on their windows and doors.

claims.statement: Celebration practices were recorded in ancient texts without mentioning a creature named Nian.
claims.statement_id: Praktik perayaan lebih dahulu tercatat dalam teks kuno tanpa menyebut makhluk bernama Nian.
claims.quote: Various aspects of cultural practices relating to Chinese New Year are part of the nian legend. These cultural practices are recorded in ancient texts, though none of them refer to a creature called nian.

claims.statement: According to one of the most famous legends, an extremely ferocious horned monster named Nian lived in ancient China, deep at the bottom of the sea all year, and climbed up to the shore only on New Year's Eve to devour cattle and kill people.
claims.statement_id: Menurut salah satu legenda paling terkenal, di Tiongkok kuno hidup monster bertanduk bernama Nian yang sangat garang; ia tinggal jauh di dasar laut sepanjang tahun dan naik ke pantai hanya pada malam tahun baru untuk melahap ternak dan membunuh orang.
claims.quote: According to one of the most famous legends, in ancient China there lived a horned monster named Nian who was extremely ferocious. Nian lived deep at the bottom of the sea all the year round and climbed up to the shore only on New Year's Eve to devour the cattle and kill people.

claims.statement: On every New Year's Eve, people from all villages would flee with the old and the young to the remote mountains to avoid the calamity caused by the monster Nian.
claims.statement_id: Setiap malam tahun baru, penduduk semua desa mengungsi bersama kaum tua dan muda ke pegunungan terpencil untuk menghindari bencana yang ditimbulkan monster Nian.
claims.quote: Thereupon on the day of every New Year's Eve people from all villages would flee, bringing along the old and the young, to the remote mountains so as to avoid the calamity caused by the monster Nian.

claims.statement: In this legend, the color red, flames and explosions were what Nian feared the most.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda ini, warna merah, api, dan ledakan adalah hal yang paling ditakuti Nian.
claims.quote: It turned out that the color red, flames, and explosions were what Nian feared the most.

claims.statement: When the door of the grandmother's house was thrown open and an old man in a red robe burst out laughing in the courtyard, the monster Nian was scared out of his wits and fled helter-skelter.
claims.statement_id: Ketika pintu rumah sang nenek dibuka dan seorang lelaki tua berjubah merah tertawa terbahak di halaman, monster Nian ketakutan dan lari tunggang langgang.
claims.quote: And when the door of the grandmother's house was thrown open and an old man in a red robe burst out laughing in the courtyard, the monster Nian was scared out of his wits and fled helter-skelter.

claims.statement: The villagers concluded that the old beggar was surely a celestial being come to expel calamities, and that red paper, red cloth, red candles and exploding firecrackers were magic weapons to drive out the monster Nian.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk akhirnya menyimpulkan bahwa pengemis tua itu pastilah makhluk langit yang datang mengusir bencana, dan bahwa kertas merah, kain merah, lilin merah, dan petasan adalah senjata ajaib untuk mengusir monster Nian.
claims.quote: They concluded in the end that the old beggar was surely the celestial being who came to expel the calamities and bless the people, and that red paper, red cloth, red candles, and the exploding firecracker were certainly the magic weapons to drive out the monster Nian.

claims.statement: The Yellow Dragon is the animal-form manifestation of the Yellow Emperor in Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Yellow Dragon adalah perwujudan berbentuk hewan dari Kaisar Kuning dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: The Yellow Dragon (simplified Chinese: 黄龙; traditional Chinese: 黃龍; pinyin: Huánglóng; Cantonese Yale: Wong4 Lung4)  is the zoomorphic incarnation of the Yellow Emperor of the center of the universe in Chinese religion and mythology.

claims.statement: In Wuxing, this dragon embodies the earth element.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Wuxing, naga ini melambangkan unsur bumi.
claims.quote: The Yellow Dragon is a part of Wuxing and the Four Symbols as the embodiment of the element of earth.

claims.statement: The Huainanzi chapter Tianwen xun (天文訓) says the centre (中央) is earth (土), its emperor is Huangdi (黃帝), its assistant Houtu (后土), who holds the cord and governs the four directions; its spirit is Zhenxing (鎮星) and its beast (獸) is the Yellow Dragon (黃龍).
claims.statement_id: Huainanzi bab Tianwen xun (天文訓) menyebut bahwa pusat (中央) adalah tanah (土), kaisarnya Huangdi (黃帝), pembantunya Houtu (后土) yang memegang tali dan mengatur empat penjuru; rohnya adalah Zhenxing (鎮星) dan binatangnya (獸) adalah Naga Kuning (黃龍).
claims.quote: 中央，土也，其帝黃帝，其佐后土，執繩而制四方。其神為鎮星，其獸黃龍，其音宮，其日戊己。

claims.statement: The Shiji (史記), Fengshan shu, records someone saying that Huangdi (黃帝) obtained the virtue of earth (土德) and a 黃龍 (yellow dragon) and 地螾 appeared; Xia obtained wood and an azure dragon (青龍) stopped at the suburb; Shang obtained metal, and Zhou obtained fire with a red crow (赤烏) as its sign.
claims.statement_id: Shiji (史記), Fengshan shu, mencatat ucapan seseorang bahwa Huangdi (黃帝) memperoleh kebajikan tanah (土德) dan 黃龍 serta 地螾 muncul; Xia memperoleh kebajikan kayu dan Naga Biru (青龍) singgah di pinggiran kota; Shang memperoleh logam, dan Zhou memperoleh api dengan pertanda burung merah (赤烏).
claims.quote: 或曰：「黃帝得土德，黃龍地螾見。夏得木德，青龍止於郊，草木暢茂。殷得金德，銀自山溢。周得火德，有赤烏之符。

claims.statement: The Shiji records that Gongsun Chen (公孫臣) of Lu submitted a memorial: Qin had obtained the virtue of water and Han should take the virtue of earth (土德), whose response is the appearance of a yellow dragon (黃龍見); he proposed changing the calendar and the colour of dress, and honouring yellow.
claims.statement_id: Shiji mencatat bahwa Gongsun Chen (公孫臣) dari Lu mengajukan surat: Qin memperoleh kebajikan air dan Han sepatutnya menerima kebajikan tanah (土德); tanggapan atas kebajikan tanah adalah munculnya naga kuning (黃龍見), sehingga ia mengusulkan agar kalender dan warna busana diubah dan warna kuning dijunjung.
claims.quote: 魯人公孫臣上書曰：「始秦得水德，今漢受之，推終始傳，則漢當土德，土德之應黃龍見。宜改正朔，易服色，色上黃。」

claims.statement: The Shiji records that three years later a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji (成紀); Emperor Wen (文帝) then summoned Gongsun Chen, appointed him an erudite (博士), and with the scholars drafted changes to the calendar and the colour of dress.
claims.statement_id: Shiji mencatat bahwa tiga tahun kemudian naga kuning muncul di Chengji (成紀); Kaisar Wen (文帝) lalu memanggil Gongsun Chen, mengangkatnya sebagai cendekiawan (博士), dan bersama para sarjana menyusun perubahan kalender dan warna busana.
claims.quote: 後三歲，黃龍見成紀。文帝乃召公孫臣，拜為博士，與諸生草改歷服色事。

claims.statement: Hundun is a faceless legendary being and an image of primordial chaos in Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Hundun adalah makhluk tanpa wajah sekaligus gambaran kekacauan purba dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Hundun (Chinese: 混沌; pinyin: Hùndùn; Wade–Giles: Hun4-tun4; lit. 'muddled confusion') is both a "legendary faceless being" in Chinese mythology and the "primordial and central chaos" in Chinese cosmogony, comparable with the world egg.

claims.statement: The term hundun also developed senses of disorder or unintelligibility.
claims.statement_id: Istilah hundun juga berkembang menjadi kata untuk keadaan kacau atau tak terpahami.
claims.quote: Hundun 混沌 was semantically extended from a mythic "primordial chaos; nebulous state of the universe before heaven and earth separated" to mean "unintelligible; chaotic; messy; mentally dense; innocent as a child".

claims.statement: Its written name has variants in the Zhuangzi and Zuozhuan.
claims.statement_id: Tulisan namanya memiliki varian dalam Zhuangzi dan Zuozhuan.
claims.quote: While hùndùn "primordial chaos" is usually written as 混沌 in contemporary sources, it is also written as 渾沌—as in the Daoist classic Zhuangzi—or 渾敦 —as in the Zuozhuan.

claims.statement: In a Zhuangzi tale, Hundun rules the central region and generously hosts Shu and Hu.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Zhuangzi, Hundun menjadi penguasa wilayah tengah yang menjamu Shu dan Hu.
claims.quote: The emperor of the South Sea was called Shu [Brief], the emperor of the North Sea was called Hu [Sudden], and the emperor of the central region was called Hun-tun [Chaos]. Shu and Hu from time to time came together for a meeting in the territory of Hun-tun, and Hun-tun treated them very generously. Shu and Hu discussed how they could repay his kindness.

claims.statement: Shu and Hu bore openings into Hun-tun each day, causing his death on the seventh day.
claims.statement_id: Mereka membuat lubang lain setiap hari, dan Hundun mati pada hari ketujuh.
claims.quote: Every day they bored another hole, and on the seventh day Hun-tun died.

claims.statement: Another account resembles a yellow sack with six feet, four wings, and no face.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran lain menyerupai kantong kuning dengan enam kaki, empat sayap, dan tanpa wajah.
claims.quote: There is a god here who looks like a yellow sack. He is scarlet like cinnabar fire. He has six feet and four wings. He is Muddle Thick. He has no face and no eyes. He knows how to sing and dance. He is in truth the great god Long River.

claims.statement: The Zuozhuan (Wengong 18) says that the Di Hong clan (帝鴻氏) had an untalented son who liked to practise wicked conduct, and the people called him Hundun (渾敦).
claims.statement_id: Zuozhuan (Wengong 18) menyebut bahwa klan Di Hong (帝鴻氏) memiliki seorang putra yang tidak berbakat, yang suka melakukan kekejian, dan rakyat menyebutnya Hundun (渾敦).
claims.quote: 昔帝鴻氏有不才子，掩義隱賊，好行凶德，醜類惡物，頑嚚不友，是與比周，天下之民，謂之渾敦

claims.statement: The Zuozhuan (Wengong 18) says that Shun, serving Yao, banished four wicked clans, Hundun, Qiongqi, Taowu, and Taotie, to the four borders to ward off chimei (螭魅).
claims.statement_id: Zuozhuan (Wengong 18) menyebut bahwa Shun, saat melayani Yao, mengusir empat klan jahat, yaitu Hundun, Qiongqi, Taowu, dan Taotie, ke empat tepi dunia untuk menangkal chimei (螭魅).
claims.quote: 舜臣堯，賓于四門，流四凶族，渾敦，窮奇，檮杌，饕餮，投諸四裔，以禦螭魅

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing (Xishan jing) records on Mount Tianshan a deity shaped like a yellow sack, red like cinnabar fire, with six feet and four wings, a hundun (渾敦) with no face or eyes, who can sing and dance, and who is in truth Dijiang (帝江).
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing (Xishan jing) mencatat di gunung Tianshan seorang dewa yang rupanya seperti kantong kuning, merah seperti api cinnabar, berkaki enam dan bersayap empat, "hundun" (渾敦) tanpa wajah dan mata, pandai menyanyi dan menari, dan sebenarnya adalah Dijiang (帝江).
claims.quote: 曰天山，多金玉，有青雄黃。英水出焉，而西南流注于湯谷。有神焉，其狀如黃囊，赤如丹火 ... 六足四翼，渾敦無面目，是識歌舞，實為帝江也

claims.statement: Wind Horse is a flying-horse image symbolizing the soul in East and Central Asian traditions.
claims.statement_id: Wind Horse adalah gambaran kuda terbang yang melambangkan jiwa dalam tradisi Asia Timur dan Tengah.
claims.quote: The wind horse is a flying horse that is the symbol of the human soul in the shamanistic tradition of East Asia and Central Asia. In Tibetan Buddhism, it was included as the pivotal element in the center of the four animals symbolizing the cardinal directions and a symbol of the idea of well-being or good fortune.

claims.statement: In Tibetan Buddhism, the horse also symbolizes well-being and good fortune.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Buddhisme Tibet, kuda ini juga menjadi lambang kesejahteraan dan keberuntungan.
claims.quote: The wind horse is a flying horse that is the symbol of the human soul in the shamanistic tradition of East Asia and Central Asia. In Tibetan Buddhism, it was included as the pivotal element in the center of the four animals symbolizing the cardinal directions and a symbol of the idea of well-being or good fortune.

claims.statement: Karmay explains that Wind Horse is predominantly an element of Tibetan folk culture.
claims.statement_id: Karmay menjelaskan bahwa Wind Horse terutama merupakan unsur budaya rakyat Tibet.
claims.quote: Windhorse was predominantly a feature of the folk culture, a "mundane notion of the layman rather than a Buddhist religious ideal," as Tibetan scholar Samten G. Karmay explains.

claims.statement: The term Wind Horse denotes good fortune beyond the flags placed in high locations.
claims.statement_id: Istilah Wind Horse mengacu pada keberuntungan, selain bendera yang dipasang di tempat tinggi.
claims.quote: Windhorse has several meanings in the Tibetan context. As Karmay notes, "the word [windhorse] is still and often mistakenly taken to mean only the actual flag planted on the roof of a house or on a high place near a village. In fact, it is a symbol of the idea of well-being or good fortune.

claims.statement: According to Clarke Warren, lungta is Tibetan for windhorse; the term carries many levels of significance, from the popular expression of folk religion to the deepest levels of spirituality, and links the two. It holds a prominent place in Tibetan religious and folk culture and has equivalents in many other cultures.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Clarke Warren, lungta adalah kata Tibet untuk windhorse; sebutan itu mengandung banyak tingkat makna, dari ungkapan agama rakyat hingga tingkat kerohanian terdalam, dan menghubungkan keduanya. Ia menempati kedudukan penting dalam budaya religius dan rakyat Tibet serta memiliki padanan di banyak budaya lain.
claims.quote: Lungta is Tibetan for windhorse. It is a designation which carries a number of levels of significance, from the popular expression of folk religion to the deepest levels of spirituality, and it links the two. It holds a prominent place in Tibetan religious and folk culture, and has its equivalents in many other cultures.

claims.statement: Warren notes that the prayer flags themselves are called lungta and are inscribed with drawings of the windhorse, accompanied in the cardinal directions by four other animals, each with its own symbolic significance (Tiger, Lion or Yak, Garuda, Dragon).
claims.statement_id: Warren menyebut bahwa bendera doa sendiri disebut lungta dan diberi gambar windhorse, yang di arah mata angin ditemani empat hewan lain, masing-masing bermakna simbolis (Harimau, Singa atau Yak, Garuda, Naga).
claims.quote: the prayer flags themselves are referred to as lungta, and are inscribed with drawings of the windhorse, accompanied in the cardinal directions by four other animals, each with its own symbolic significance (Tiger, Lion or Yak, Garuda, Dragon).

claims.statement: Warren writes that the popular explanation of lungta is "good fortune" or "luck", but he calls "luck" a shallow sense; windhorse refers to something much more basic and vital than mere "luck" in the Western sense of the word.
claims.statement_id: Warren menulis bahwa penjelasan populer menyebut lungta berarti "keberuntungan" atau "nasib baik", tetapi menurutnya "keberuntungan" hanyalah makna yang dangkal; windhorse merujuk pada sesuatu yang jauh lebih mendasar dan vital daripada sekadar "keberuntungan" dalam pengertian Barat.
claims.quote: The popular explanation of lungta is that it refers to “good fortune” or “luck”. Surprisingly, a fair amount of the academic literature on Tibetan culture stops at this (with notable exceptions). But “luck” is a shallow sense of lungta. Windhorse refers to something much more basic and vital than mere “luck”, at least in the Western sense of the word.

claims.statement: Warren says that Samten Karmay, in a brief paper titled Windhorse and the Well-being of Man, traces windhorse's possible roots to China (where it may have been confounded with "river-horse") and, in a later and more Buddhist context, to India.
claims.statement_id: Warren menyebut bahwa Samten Karmay, dalam makalah singkat berjudul Windhorse and the Well-being of Man, menelusuri kemungkinan akar windhorse ke Tiongkok (tempat ia mungkin tertukar dengan "kuda sungai") dan, pada konteks yang lebih belakangan dan lebih Buddhis, ke India.
claims.quote: Samten Karmay, in an excellent brief paper on the origins of windhorse, entitled Windhorse and the Well-being of Man*, traces its possible roots to China, on one hand, (where it may have been confounded with “river-horse”, another potent image and principle) and to India in another later, more Buddhist context.

claims.statement: Warren writes that a person's lungta registers their relative synchronization with their own body and mind and the world around them, so lungta also has a protective function when successfully invoked.
claims.statement_id: Warren menulis bahwa lungta seseorang mencerminkan keselarasannya dengan tubuh, pikiran, dan dunia di sekitarnya, sehingga lungta juga memiliki fungsi pelindung bila berhasil diundang.
claims.quote: A person’s lungta is a register of their relative synchronization with their own body and mind, and the world around them. So in this regard, lungta also has a protective function when successfully invoked.

claims.statement: Jin Chan is the golden toad in Chinese tradition, used as a feng shui prosperity charm.
claims.statement_id: Jin Chan adalah kodok emas dalam tradisi Tiongkok yang dipakai sebagai lambang kemakmuran feng shui.
claims.quote: The Jin Chan (Chinese: 金蟾; pinyin: jīn chán; lit. 'Golden Toad'), also called Chan Chuy (Chinese: 蟾蜍; pinyin: chánchú; lit. 'Toad') or "Zhaocai Chan Chu" (Chinese: 招财蟾蜍; pinyin: zhāocái chánchú; lit. 'wealth-beckoning toad'), is most commonly translated as "Money Toad" or "Money Frog". It represents a popular feng shui charm for prosperity.

claims.statement: The tale places its appearance at a full moon near places about to receive good news.
claims.statement_id: Kisah menyebut kemunculannya saat bulan purnama dekat tempat yang akan menerima kabar baik.
claims.quote: This mythical creature is said to appear during the full moon, near houses or businesses that will soon receive good news (most of the time, the nature of this good news is understood to be wealth-related).

claims.statement: Its portrayal includes red eyes, three legs, and a coin in its mouth.
claims.statement_id: Penggambarannya mencakup mata merah, tiga kaki, dan koin di mulut.
claims.quote: The Jin Chan is usually depicted as a bullfrog with red eyes, flared nostrils and only one hind leg (for a total of three legs), sitting on a pile of traditional Chinese cash, with a coin in its mouth. On its back, it often displays seven diamond spots. According to feng shui beliefs, Jin Chan helps attract and protect wealth, and guards against bad luck.

claims.statement: In feng shui belief, Jin Chan attracts and protects wealth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam feng shui, Jin Chan dipercaya menarik dan melindungi kekayaan.
claims.quote: The Jin Chan is usually depicted as a bullfrog with red eyes, flared nostrils and only one hind leg (for a total of three legs), sitting on a pile of traditional Chinese cash, with a coin in its mouth. On its back, it often displays seven diamond spots. According to feng shui beliefs, Jin Chan helps attract and protect wealth, and guards against bad luck.

claims.statement: The money toad is associated with Liu Haichan as the immortal's animal companion.
claims.statement_id: Kodok uang ini dihubungkan dengan Liu Haichan sebagai pendamping hewan sang xian.
claims.quote: The Jin Chan is a legendary animal of the Han people. The money toad is associated with the Daoist monk, Liu Haichan, as the xianren's animal companion.

claims.statement: The Cleveland Museum of Art describes Liu Haichan as a Daoist immortal sometimes included among the Eight Immortals, said to have lived during the Five Dynasties period (907–979) and to have left his position as a grand councilor to become a hermit.
claims.statement_id: Museum Seni Cleveland menyebut Liu Haichan sebagai tokoh abadi Tao yang kadang dimasukkan dalam Delapan Dewa Abadi, yang dikatakan hidup pada periode Lima Dinasti (907–979) dan meninggalkan jabatannya sebagai penasihat agung untuk menjadi pertapa.
claims.quote: Liu Haichan is a Daoist immortal sometimes included among the Eight Immortals. He was said to have lived during the Five Dynasties period (907–979) and left his position as a grand councilor to become a hermit.

claims.statement: According to the museum, Liu Haichan is usually depicted carrying a string of coins and accompanied by a three-legged toad; he became a god of wealth and his toad symbolizes wealth as well.
claims.statement_id: Menurut museum itu, Liu Haichan biasanya digambarkan membawa untaian koin dan ditemani kodok berkaki tiga; ia menjadi dewa kekayaan dan kodoknya pun melambangkan kekayaan.
claims.quote: Usually depicted carrying a string of coins and accompanied by a three-legged toad, Liu Haichan became a god of wealth and his toad symbolizes wealth as well.

claims.statement: A gallery label at the Nelson-Atkins Museum for a woodblock print says the boy on the right represents the Daoist immortal Liu Hai playing with his pet, a three-legged toad, and that Liu Hai was deemed to be a spirit of wealth.
claims.statement_id: Label galeri Museum Nelson-Atkins pada sebuah cetakan kayu menyebut anak di sisi kanan mewakili tokoh abadi Tao Liu Hai yang bermain dengan hewan peliharaannya, kodok berkaki tiga, dan Liu Hai dianggap sebagai roh kekayaan.
claims.quote: The boy on the right represents the Daoist immortal, Liu Hai, playing with his pet, a three-legged toad. Liu Hai was deemed to be a spirit of wealth.

claims.statement: Kuafu is a giant in Chinese mythology who seeks to capture the sun.
claims.statement_id: Kuafu adalah raksasa mitologi Tiongkok yang ingin menangkap matahari.
claims.quote: Kuafu (Chinese: 夸父) is a giant in Chinese mythology who wished to capture the Sun.  He was a grandson of Houtu.

claims.statement: Kuafu is described as Houtu's grandson.
claims.statement_id: Kuafu disebut cucu Houtu.
claims.quote: Kuafu (Chinese: 夸父) is a giant in Chinese mythology who wished to capture the Sun.  He was a grandson of Houtu.

claims.statement: He pursues the sun east to west and drinks from the Yellow and Wei rivers.
claims.statement_id: Ia mengejar matahari dari timur ke barat dan meminum Sungai Kuning serta Sungai Wei.
claims.quote: Kuafu is a giant. One day, Kuafu decided to chase and catch the Sun. He followed the Sun from the East to the West, draining the Yellow River and the Wei River (all rivers and lakes crossing his path) to quench his burning thirst. However, the big rivers were also unable to quench his thirst, and as he searched for more water, he eventually died of dehydration.

claims.statement: The river water cannot quench his thirst, and he dies from dehydration.
claims.statement_id: Air sungai tidak menghilangkan hausnya dan ia mati akibat kekurangan air.
claims.quote: Kuafu is a giant. One day, Kuafu decided to chase and catch the Sun. He followed the Sun from the East to the West, draining the Yellow River and the Wei River (all rivers and lakes crossing his path) to quench his burning thirst. However, the big rivers were also unable to quench his thirst, and as he searched for more water, he eventually died of dehydration.

claims.statement: His wooden club becomes a forest of peach trees.
claims.statement_id: Tongkat kayunya berubah menjadi hutan pohon persik.
claims.quote: The wooden club he was carrying grew into a vast forest of peach trees called the Deng Forest (鄧林).

claims.statement: Another version describes his body becoming a mountain range.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain mengisahkan tubuhnya menjadi pegunungan.
claims.quote: In one version, Kuafu turns into a mountain range. This mountain range and the peach forest are said to be located in present day Lingbao.

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing (Great Wilderness, North) records a man named Kuafu in the Great Wilderness who wears two yellow snakes at his ears and holds two yellow snakes; Houtu begot Xin, and Xin begot Kuafu.
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing (Dahuang Bei Jing) mencatat seorang bernama Kuafu di Dahuang, yang mengenakan dua ular kuning di telinga dan memegang dua ular kuning; Houtu melahirkan Xin, dan Xin melahirkan Kuafu.
claims.quote: 大荒之中，有山名曰成都載天。有人珥兩黄蛇，把兩黄蛇，名曰夸父。后土生信，信生夸父。

claims.statement: In the Dahuang Bei Jing, Kuafu, who overestimated his strength, sought to chase the sun's shadow and overtook it at Yugu; he tried to drink from the river but it was not enough, headed for the great marsh, and died before reaching it. The same text also says Yinglong had killed Chiyou and then Kuafu.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Dahuang Bei Jing, Kuafu yang tidak menakar kekuatannya hendak mengejar bayangan matahari dan menyusulnya di Yugu; ia hendak minum dari sungai tetapi tidak cukup, menuju rawa besar, dan wafat sebelum sampai. Teks yang sama juga menyebut Yinglong telah membunuh Chiyou dan lalu Kuafu.
claims.quote: 夸父不量力，欲追日景，逮之于禺谷。將飲河而不足也，將走大澤，未至，死于此。應龍已殺蚩尤，又殺夸父，乃去南方處之，故南方多雨。

claims.statement: In the Haiwai Bei Jing, Kuafu races the sun and grows thirsty; he drinks from the He and Wei rivers, which are not enough, heads north to drink at the great marsh, and dies of thirst on the way; the staff he discarded turns into the Deng forest.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Haiwai Bei Jing, Kuafu berlomba lari dengan matahari lalu haus; ia minum dari Sungai He dan Sungai Wei yang tidak cukup, hendak minum di rawa besar di utara, tetapi mati kehausan di tengah jalan, dan tongkat yang ia buang menjadi hutan Deng.
claims.quote: 夸父與日逐走，入日。渴，欲得飲，飲於河、渭，河、渭不足，北飲大澤。未至，道渴而死。棄其杖，化為鄧林。

claims.statement: Ungnyeo is the bear-woman in the Korean nation’s creation myth.
claims.statement_id: Ungnyeo adalah perempuan beruang dalam mitos penciptaan bangsa Korea.
claims.quote: was a bear who became a woman according to the creation myth of the Korean nation. She has an important role in the myth as the wife of Hwanung, the divine king of the world, and as the mother of Dangun, the mythological founder of Korea.

claims.statement: She becomes Hwanung's wife and Dangun's mother.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi istri Hwanung dan ibu Dangun.
claims.quote: She has an important role in the myth as the wife of Hwanung, the divine king of the world, and as the mother of Dangun, the mythological founder of Korea.

claims.statement: Hwanung gives a bear and tiger food and instructions to avoid sunlight.
claims.statement_id: Hwanung memberi beruang dan harimau makanan serta larangan terkena matahari.
claims.quote: In the tale, a tiger and a bear lived together in a cave and prayed to the divine king Hwanung to be made human. Hwanung heard their prayers and gave them each 20 cloves of garlic and a bundle of mugwort, and ordered them to stay out of the sunlight and eat only this food for 100 days. Due to hunger, the tiger left the cave after roughly 20 days, but the bear remained inside.

claims.statement: The tiger leaves the cave, while the bear remains and becomes a woman.
claims.statement_id: Harimau meninggalkan gua, tetapi beruang bertahan lalu berubah menjadi perempuan.
claims.quote: Due to hunger, the tiger left the cave after roughly 20 days, but the bear remained inside. After 21 days, she was transformed into a woman.

claims.statement: Ungnyeo prays beneath a sacred tree for a child.
claims.statement_id: Ungnyeo berdoa di bawah pohon suci untuk memperoleh anak.
claims.quote: Ungnyeo was grateful and made offerings to Hwanung. Her lack of a husband drove her to depression, and she began to pray beneath a sacred betula tree ... to be blessed with a child. Hwanung heard her prayers and was deeply moved. He took Ungnyeo as his wife and soon after, she gave birth to a son, Dangun, who would go on to found the nation of Korea.

claims.statement: The founding account appears in the Samguk Yusa written by Ilyon.
claims.statement_id: Kisah pendirian ini tercatat dalam Samguk Yusa yang ditulis Ilyon.
claims.quote: The earliest form of the myth is found at the beginning of the Samguk Yusa, a part-mythological, part-historical chronicle of Korea’s Three Kingdoms Period (primarily focusing on the kingdom of Silla).  It was written by the Buddhist monk Ilyon during the late 13th century CE, while the Korean Peninsula was under Mongol rule.

claims.statement: The Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) says a bear and a tiger lived in the same cave and kept praying to the divine 雄 (Ung) to become human; the god gave a bundle of 靈艾 (mugwort) and twenty cloves of garlic (蒜二十枚) and told them that if they ate these and did not see sunlight for a hundred days (百日) they would obtain human form.
claims.statement_id: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) menyebut seekor beruang dan seekor harimau tinggal di gua yang sama dan terus memohon kepada sang dewa 雄 (Ung) agar menjadi manusia; sang dewa memberi seikat 靈艾 (artemisia) dan dua puluh siung bawang putih (蒜二十枚), dan berkata bahwa bila mereka memakannya dan tidak melihat sinar matahari selama seratus hari (百日), mereka akan memperoleh wujud manusia.
claims.quote: 有一熊一虎，同穴而居，常祈于神雄。願化為​人。時神遺靈艾一炷。蒜二十枚曰。爾輩食之。不見日光百日。便得人形。

claims.statement: The Samguk Yusa says the bear and the tiger ate it; for 三七日 (three times seven days) the bear kept the abstention and obtained a woman's body (女身), while the tiger could not keep it and did not obtain a human body. The bear-woman (熊女) had no one to marry.
claims.statement_id: Samguk Yusa menyebut bahwa beruang dan harimau memakannya; selama 三七日 (tiga kali tujuh hari) beruang berpantang dan memperoleh tubuh perempuan (女身), sedangkan harimau tidak mampu berpantang dan tidak memperoleh tubuh manusia. Perempuan beruang (熊女) itu tidak punya pasangan untuk dinikahi.
claims.quote: 熊虎得而食之。忌三七日。熊得女身。虎不能忌。而不得人身。熊女者無與為婚。

claims.statement: The Samguk Yusa says the bear-woman (熊女) kept praying beneath the altar tree (壇樹) to conceive; the god 雄 (Ung) took a temporary changed form (假化) and married her, and she bore a son called 壇君王儉.
claims.statement_id: Samguk Yusa menyebut bahwa perempuan beruang (熊女) setiap kali berdoa di bawah pohon altar (壇樹) agar mengandung; sang dewa 雄 (Ung) berubah wujud sementara (假化) dan menikahinya, ia melahirkan seorang putra yang bergelar 壇君王儉.
claims.quote: 熊女者無與為婚。故每於壇樹下咒願有孕。雄乃假化而婚之。孕生子。號曰壇君王儉。

claims.statement: Yinglong is a winged dragon and rain deity of ancient Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Yinglong adalah naga bersayap dan dewa hujan dalam mitologi Tiongkok kuno.
claims.quote: Yinglong (traditional Chinese: 應龍; simplified Chinese: 应龙; pinyin: yìnglóng; lit. 'responsive dragon') is a winged dragon and rain deity in ancient Chinese mythology.

claims.statement: Classical texts associate it with the Yellow Emperor and King Yu.
claims.statement_id: Teks klasik menghubungkannya dengan Kaisar Kuning dan Raja Yu.
claims.quote: The Chinese classics frequently mention yinglong 應龍 "a winged rain-dragon" in myths about the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, especially the Yellow Emperor and his alleged descendant King Yu. The examples below, limited to books with English translations, are roughly arranged in chronological order, although some heterogeneous texts have uncertain dates of composition.

claims.statement: The Chu Ci mentions Yinglong helping Yu control the great deluge.
claims.statement_id: Chu Ci menyebut Yinglong membantu Yu mengendalikan banjir besar.
claims.quote: The (3rd–2nd centuries BCE) Chu Ci "Songs of Chu" mentions Yinglong helping King Yu 禹, the legendary founder of the Xia dynasty, to control the mythic Great Deluge. According to Chinese mythology, Emperor Yao 堯 assigned Yu's father Gun 鯀, who was supposedly a descendant of the Yellow Emperor, to control massive flooding, but he failed.

claims.statement: The Heavenly Questions section discusses Yinglong among cosmological questions.
claims.statement_id: Bagian Heavenly Questions membahas Yinglong dalam rangkaian pertanyaan kosmologis.
claims.quote: The Heavenly Questions section (3, 天問) asks about Yinglong, in context with Zhulong 燭龍 "Torch Dragon".

claims.statement: The poem asks what the winged dragon traced on the ground and where seas and rivers flowed.
claims.statement_id: Puisi itu menanyakan apa yang digoreskan naga bersayap pada tanah saat penanganan banjir.
claims.quote: What did the winged dragon trace on the ground? Where did the seas and rivers flow?

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing (Dahuang Beijing) says Yinglong, having killed Chiyou and also Kuafu, went off to dwell in the south, which is why the south has much rain.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Shanhaijing (Dahuang Beijing), Yinglong disebut sudah membunuh Chiyou dan juga Kuafu, lalu pergi menetap di selatan, sehingga selatan banyak hujan.
claims.quote: 夸父不量力，欲追日景，逮之于禺谷。將飲河而不足也，將走大澤，未至，死于此。應龍已殺蚩尤，又殺夸父，乃去南方處之，故南方多雨。

claims.statement: In the Shanhaijing (Dahuang Beijing), when Chiyou made weapons and attacked the Yellow Emperor, the emperor ordered Yinglong to attack him in the fields of Jizhou, and Yinglong stored up water.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Shanhaijing (Dahuang Beijing), ketika Chiyou membuat senjata dan menyerang Kaisar Kuning, sang kaisar memerintahkan Yinglong menyerangnya di padang Jizhou, dan Yinglong menampung air.
claims.quote: 蚩尤作兵伐黄帝，黄帝乃令應龍攻之冀州之野。應龍畜水。蚩尤請風伯雨師，縱大風雨。

claims.statement: In the Shanhaijing (Dahuang Dongjing), Yinglong killed Chiyou and Kuafu and could not go back up; so droughts came often below, and making a figure in the shape of Yinglong during drought brought heavy rain.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Shanhaijing (Dahuang Dongjing), Yinglong disebut membunuh Chiyou dan Kuafu serta tidak dapat naik kembali; karena itu sering terjadi kekeringan di bawah, dan orang yang membuat rupa Yinglong saat kemarau memperoleh hujan lebat.
claims.quote: 應龍出 ... 南極，殺蚩尤與夸父，不得復上。故下數旱，旱而為應龍之狀，乃得大雨。

claims.statement: Peng is a giant Chinese mythological bird transformed from the fish Kun.
claims.statement_id: Peng adalah burung raksasa dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang berubah dari ikan Kun.
claims.quote: A Peng (Chinese: 鵬; pinyin: péng) or Dapeng (大鵬; dàpéng) is a giant bird that transforms from a Kun (鯤; kūn), a giant fish, in Chinese mythology.

claims.statement: The peng character uses a bird component, while kun uses a fish component.
claims.statement_id: Aksara peng memakai unsur burung, sedangkan kun memakai unsur ikan.
claims.quote: The Chinese logograms for peng and kun exemplify common radical-phonetic characters. Peng (鵬) combines the "bird radical" (鳥) with a peng (朋; 'friend') phonetic, and kun (鲲; 鯤) combines the "fish radical" (魚) with a kun (昆; 'progeny', 'insect') phonetic.

claims.statement: Peng was formerly used as a character variant for feng in fenghuang.
claims.statement_id: Peng dahulu juga dipakai sebagai varian aksara feng dalam fenghuang.
claims.quote: Both the mythic Chinese Peng and Kun names involve word play. Peng (鵬) was anciently a variant Chinese character for feng (鳳) in fenghuang (鳳凰; "Chinese phoenix"), as in the ca. 100 CE Shuowen Jiezi; Kun (鯤) originally meant "fish roe; fry; spawn" (ca. 200 BCE Erya).

claims.statement: Dapeng and Dapengniao are alternative names denoting the great Peng or great Peng bird.
claims.statement_id: Dapeng dan Dapengniao termasuk sebutan lain yang berarti Peng besar atau burung Peng besar.
claims.quote: Synonyms of Peng include Dapeng (大鵬; "Big Peng", "Great Peng") and Dapengniao (大鵬鳥; "Great Peng Bird"). Dapeng is also a place name for a few places in greater China, most notably in Shenzhen and Taiwan.

claims.statement: In the "Xiaoyao You" chapter of the Zhuangzi, a fish named Kun lives in the Northern Darkness and is immensely large; it transforms into a bird named Peng, whose back spans thousands of li and whose wings are like clouds hanging from the sky.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab "Xiaoyao You" Zhuangzi, di Lautan Utara ada ikan bernama Kun yang sangat besar; ikan itu berubah menjadi burung bernama Peng, yang punggungnya luas ribuan li dan sayapnya bagai awan yang menggantung dari langit.
claims.quote: 北冥有魚，其名爲鯤。鯤之大，不知其幾千里也，化而爲鳥，其名爲鵬。鵬之背，不知其幾千里也，怒而飛，其翼若垂天之雲。

claims.statement: When the sea stirs, the bird will migrate to the Southern Darkness, the Pool of Heaven; Qi Xie, "one who records the strange", says that in the migration it beats the water for three thousand li.
claims.statement_id: Ketika laut bergolak, burung itu akan berpindah ke Lautan Selatan, yaitu Telaga Langit; Qi Xie, "pencatat hal-hal ganjil", berkata bahwa dalam perpindahan itu ia memukul air sejauh tiga ribu li.
claims.quote: 是鳥也，海運，則將徙於南冥。南冥者，天池也。齊諧者，志怪者也。諧之言曰：「鵬之徙於南冥也，水擊三千里

claims.statement: A small quail laughs at the Peng, saying that it only leaps up a few ren before coming down and flies among the brambles, and asking where the Peng is going.
claims.statement_id: Seekor burung puyuh kecil menertawakan Peng, sambil berkata bahwa ia sendiri hanya melompat naik beberapa ren lalu turun dan terbang di antara semak, dan bertanya ke mana Peng hendak pergi.
claims.quote: 斥鴳笑之曰：「彼且奚適也？我騰躍而上，不過數仞而下，翺翔蓬蒿之間，此亦飛之至也。而彼且奚適也？」

claims.statement: Xiangliu is a venomous nine-headed serpent monster bringing floods in Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Xiangliu adalah monster ular berbisa berkepala sembilan yang membawa banjir dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: is a venomous nine-headed snake monster that brings floods and destruction in Chinese mythology.

claims.statement: In the Shanhaijing, it is known as Xiangyao.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Shanhaijing, ia dikenal sebagai Xiangyao.
claims.quote: known in the Classic of Mountains and Seas as Xiangyao

claims.statement: Older woodcuts cluster its heads on a single neck.
claims.statement_id: Cetakan kayu lama menempatkan kepala-kepalanya mengelompok pada satu leher.
claims.quote: Xiangliu may be depicted with his body coiled on itself. The nine heads are arranged differently in different representations. Modern depictions resemble the hydra, with each head on a separate neck. Older wood-cuts show the heads clustered on a single neck, either side-by-side or in a stack three high, facing three directions.

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing describes Xiangliu as a subordinate of the water deity Gonggong.
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing menyebut Xiangliu sebagai bawahan dewa air Gonggong.
claims.quote: According to the Classic of Mountains and Seas (Shanhaijing), Xiangliu (Xiangyao) was a minister of the snake-like water deity Gonggong. Xiangliu devastated the ecology everywhere he went. He was so gluttonous that all nine heads would feed at the same meal.

claims.statement: Places it touches or breathes upon become bogs of poisonous bitter water.
claims.statement_id: Tempat yang disentuh atau diembusnya menjadi rawa berair pahit beracun.
claims.quote: Everywhere he rested or breathed upon (or that his tongue touched, depending on the telling) became boggy with poisonously bitter water, devoid of human and animal life.

claims.statement: An interpretation quoted by Eberhard compares Xiangliu with an eel in flood tales.
claims.statement_id: Penafsiran yang dikutip Eberhard membandingkan Xiangliu dengan belut dalam kisah banjir.
claims.quote: Sun points out that the eel is a most important animal in the flood tales of Formosan aborigines. Ying-lung, who ...

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing (山海經), Haiwai bei jing, says Gonggong's (共工) minister is named Xiangliu (相柳氏), has nine heads (九首) and eats from nine mountains; where it reaches (所抵) there become marshes and watery valleys (澤谿); Yu (禹) killed it and its blood was foul, so the five grains could not be planted there.
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing (山海經), Haiwai bei jing, menyebut menteri Gonggong (共工) bernama Xiangliu (相柳氏) berkepala sembilan (九首) yang makan di sembilan gunung; tempat yang dijangkaunya (所抵) menjadi rawa dan lembah berair (澤谿); Yu (禹) membunuhnya dan darahnya berbau amis sehingga lima jenis biji-bijian tidak dapat ditanam di sana.
claims.quote: 共工之臣曰相柳氏，九首，以食于九山。相柳之所抵，厥為澤谿。禹殺相柳，其血腥，不可以樹五穀種。

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing, Haiwai bei jing, describes Xiangliu as nine-headed with human faces (九首人面) and a blue snake body (蛇身而青); the text adds the phrase "dares not shoot northward" (不敢北射), in awe of Gonggong's terrace (共工之臺); the terrace is square and at a corner there is a tiger-coloured snake whose head faces south.
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing, Haiwai bei jing, menggambarkan Xiangliu sebagai makhluk berkepala sembilan dan berwajah manusia (九首人面), bertubuh ular berwarna biru (蛇身而青); teks menambahkan frasa "tidak berani memanah ke utara" (不敢北射) karena segan pada menara Gonggong (共工之臺); menara itu persegi empat dan di sudutnya ada seekor ular berwarna harimau yang kepalanya menghadap ke selatan.
claims.quote: 相柳者，九首人面，蛇身而青。不敢北射，畏共工之臺。臺在其東，臺四方，隅有一蛇，虎色，首衝南方。

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing, Dahuang bei jing, names a minister of Gonggong as Xiangyao (相繇), with nine heads and a snake body, coiling itself (自環) and eating from nine lands (九土); where it passes the places become springs and marshes whose water is bitter (不辛乃苦), so no beast can live there. Yu dammed the floods and killed it; its blood was rank, grain could not grow, and the land was too watery to inhabit.
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing, Dahuang bei jing, menyebut menteri Gonggong bernama Xiangyao (相繇) berkepala sembilan dan bertubuh ular, melingkar sendiri (自環) dan makan di sembilan negeri (九土); tempat yang dikenainya menjadi mata air dan rawa yang rasanya pahit (不辛乃苦) sehingga tak satu pun binatang dapat tinggal di sana. Yu membendung banjir dan membunuhnya; darahnya amis dan busuk, biji-bijian tak dapat tumbuh, dan tanahnya terlalu berair untuk dihuni.
claims.quote: 共工臣名曰相繇，九首蛇身，自環，食于九土。其所歍所尼，即為源澤，不辛乃苦，百獸莫能處。禹湮洪水，殺相繇，其血腥臭，不可生榖；其地多水，不可居也。

claims.statement: Korean dragons are legendary creatures of Korean mythology and folklore.
claims.statement_id: Naga Korea adalah makhluk legenda dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Korea.
claims.quote: Korean dragons (Korean: 용/룡) are legendary creatures in Korean mythology and folklore. It is also called Mir (미르) or Miri (미리) in Korean.

claims.statement: Mir or Miri are Korean names for dragons.
claims.statement_id: Mir atau Miri termasuk nama naga dalam bahasa Korea.
claims.quote: Korean dragons (Korean: 용/룡) are legendary creatures in Korean mythology and folklore. It is also called Mir (미르) or Miri (미리) in Korean.

claims.statement: These dragons are primarily associated with water, agriculture, rain, and clouds.
claims.statement_id: Naga ini terutama dikaitkan dengan air, pertanian, hujan, dan awan.
claims.quote: Whereas most dragons in European mythology are linked to the elements of fire and destruction, dragons in Korean mythology are primarily benevolent beings related to water and agriculture, often considered bringers of rain and clouds. Hence, many Korean dragons are said to have resided in rivers, lakes, oceans, or even deep mountain ponds.

claims.statement: The Munmu legend recounts his wish to become an East Sea dragon protecting the kingdom.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Munmu mengisahkan keinginannya menjadi naga Laut Timur untuk melindungi kerajaan.
claims.quote: One particular Korean legend speaks of the great King Munmu, who on his deathbed wished to become a "Great dragon of the East Sea in order to protect his kingdom".

claims.statement: Korean dragons are described with longer beards than Chinese dragons.
claims.statement_id: Naga Korea digambarkan memiliki janggut lebih panjang dibanding naga Tiongkok.
claims.quote: The Korean dragon is in many ways very similar in appearance to other East Asian dragons such as the Chinese and Japanese dragons. It differs from the Chinese dragon in that it developed a longer beard.

claims.statement: Depictions may include a yeouiju orb in the claws or mouth.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran dapat menyertakan bola yeouiju pada cakar atau mulutnya.
claims.quote: Occasionally a dragon may be depicted as carrying a giant orb known as the yeouiju (여의주), the Korean name for the mythical Cintamani, in its claws or its mouth.

claims.statement: In the Samguk Yusa, a king whose will asked for burial on a great rock in the East Sea once told the Dharma master Jiui (智義) that after his death he wished to become a great dragon protecting the state, revering the Buddhist teaching and guarding the country.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Samguk Yusa, seorang raja yang berwasiat dimakamkan di batu karang besar di Laut Timur pernah berkata kepada guru Dharma Jiui (智義) bahwa setelah wafat ia ingin menjadi naga besar pelindung negara, yang memuliakan ajaran Buddha dan menjaga negerinya.
claims.quote: 遺詔葬於東海中大巖上。王平時常謂智義法師曰。朕身後願為護國大龍。崇奉佛法。守護邦家。

claims.statement: A temple record cited in the Samguk Yusa says King Munmu (文武王) began the temple to suppress the Wa (Japanese) troops, died before it was finished, and became a sea dragon; his son Sinmun (神文) completed it in the second year of the Kaiyao era.
claims.statement_id: Catatan kuil yang dikutip Samguk Yusa menyebut Raja Munmu (文武王) mulai membangun kuil itu untuk menekan pasukan Wa (Jepang), wafat sebelum selesai, dan menjadi naga laut; putranya Sinmun (神文) menyelesaikannya pada tahun kedua era Kaiyao.
claims.quote: 寺中記云。文武王欲鎮倭兵。故始創此寺。未畢而崩。為海龍。其子神文立開耀二年畢。

claims.statement: In the story of the bamboo flute, on the sixteenth day of that month, when the wind cleared and the waves calmed, the king sails to a mountain in the sea, and a dragon comes to present a black jade belt and receives him to sit together.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah seruling bambu, pada hari keenam belas bulan itu, ketika angin reda dan ombak tenang, raja berlayar menuju sebuah gunung di laut, dan seekor naga datang mempersembahkan sabuk batu giok hitam serta menyambutnya duduk bersama.
claims.quote: 至其月十六日風霽波平。王泛海入其山。有龍奉黑玉帶來獻。迎接共坐。

claims.statement: In that story, the late father of the reigning king is said to have become a great dragon in the sea and Kim Yushin (庾信) a heavenly god; together the two sages bring out a priceless treasure to be presented.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, ayah mendiang raja yang berkuasa disebut telah menjadi naga besar di laut dan Kim Yushin (庾信) menjadi dewa langit; keduanya bersepakat mengeluarkan harta tak ternilai untuk dipersembahkan.
claims.quote: 今王考為海中大龍。庾信復為天神。二聖同心。出此無價大寶。令我獻之。

claims.statement: When clouds and fog suddenly darkened the way so that the party lost its path, an official (日官) said it was a transformation of the East Sea dragon and that a good deed should be performed; once the order to build a Buddhist temple for the dragon was issued, the clouds and fog cleared.
claims.statement_id: Ketika awan dan kabut tiba-tiba menggelapkan jalan hingga rombongan tersesat, seorang pejabat (日官) berkata bahwa itu perubahan wujud naga Laut Timur dan perlu dilakukan perbuatan baik; setelah perintah mendirikan kuil Buddha untuk sang naga dikeluarkan, awan dan kabut menghilang.
claims.quote: 忽雲霧冥曀。迷失道路。怪問左右。日官奏云。此東海龍所變也。宜行勝事以解之。於是敕有司為龍刱佛寺。近境施令已出。雲開霧散。

claims.statement: The pleased East Sea dragon led seven sons to appear before the carriage, praised virtue and offered dance and music; one son followed to the capital, assisted the royal government, and was named Cheoyong (處容).
claims.statement_id: Naga Laut Timur yang senang membawa tujuh putranya muncul di depan kereta, memuji kebajikan serta mempersembahkan tarian dan musik; salah satu putranya mengikuti ke ibu kota, membantu pemerintahan, dan bernama Cheoyong (處容).
claims.quote: 東海龍喜。乃率七子現於駕前。讚德獻舞奏樂。其一子隨駕入京。輔佐王政。名曰處容。

claims.statement: At a seaside pavilion a sea dragon suddenly seized a lord's (公) wife and took her into the sea; on the advice of an old man, the people sang while striking the shore with sticks, and the dragon returned her.
claims.statement_id: Di sebuah paviliun tepi laut, naga laut tiba-tiba merenggut istri seorang bangsawan (公) dan membawanya ke laut; atas saran seorang lelaki tua, rakyat bernyanyi sambil memukul tepi pantai dengan tongkat, lalu sang naga mengembalikan sang istri.
claims.quote: 又有臨海亭。晝膳次海龍忽攬夫人入海。公顛倒躄地。計無所出。又有一老人告曰。故人有言。眾口鑠金。今海中傍生。何不畏眾口乎。宜進界內民。作歌唱之。以杖打岸。則可見夫人矣。公從之。龍奉夫人出海獻之。

claims.statement: In one story, two women say that an envoy of Tang (唐) and two men from Hexi (河西) transformed their husbands, two dragons, and the dragon of the well of Fenhuang temple (芬皇寺) into small fish and took them away in a tube; they beg that the dragons, described as dragons protecting the country, be kept in the land.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah kisah, dua perempuan berkata bahwa utusan Tang (唐) dan dua orang dari Hexi (河西) mengubah dua naga suami mereka dan naga sumur Kuil Fenhuang (芬皇寺) menjadi ikan kecil dan membawanya dalam tabung; mereka memohon agar para naga itu, yang disebut naga pelindung negara, ditahan di negeri itu.
claims.quote: 唐使將河西國二人而來。咒我夫二龍及芬皇寺井等三龍。變為小魚。筒貯而歸。願陛下敕二人。留我夫等。護國龍也。

claims.statement: Ao is a great marine turtle in Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Ao adalah kura-kura laut besar dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Ao (traditional Chinese: 鰲; simplified Chinese: 鳌; pinyin: áo < Old Chinese (ZS): *ŋaːw) is a large marine turtle in Chinese mythology. He was thought to have lived in the South China Sea during the time of the formation of the world. When the goddess Nüwa, creator of mankind, was repairing the sky after a disaster, she chopped off Ao's four legs and used them as supports.

claims.statement: It is said to inhabit the South China Sea during the world's formation.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipercaya hidup di Laut Tiongkok Selatan pada masa pembentukan dunia.
claims.quote: Ao (traditional Chinese: 鰲; simplified Chinese: 鳌; pinyin: áo < Old Chinese (ZS): *ŋaːw) is a large marine turtle in Chinese mythology. He was thought to have lived in the South China Sea during the time of the formation of the world. When the goddess Nüwa, creator of mankind, was repairing the sky after a disaster, she chopped off Ao's four legs and used them as supports.

claims.statement: Nüwa cuts off Ao's four legs to support the damaged sky.
claims.statement_id: Nüwa memotong empat kaki Ao untuk menopang langit yang rusak.
claims.quote: Ao (traditional Chinese: 鰲; simplified Chinese: 鳌; pinyin: áo < Old Chinese (ZS): *ŋaːw) is a large marine turtle in Chinese mythology. He was thought to have lived in the South China Sea during the time of the formation of the world. When the goddess Nüwa, creator of mankind, was repairing the sky after a disaster, she chopped off Ao's four legs and used them as supports.

claims.statement: Another version places it in the Bohai Sea carrying three islands of immortals on its back.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain menempatkannya di Laut Bohai membawa tiga pulau makhluk abadi pada punggung.
claims.quote: Another myth claims that Ao still lives and resides in the Bohai Sea, where he carries the three islands of the Eight Immortals (Penglai, Fangzhang, and Yingzhou) upon his back.

claims.statement: Ao is considered an influence on the dragon-turtle figure Bixi.
claims.statement_id: Ao dianggap memengaruhi tokoh Bixi yang berwujud campuran naga dan kura-kura.
claims.quote: He is thought to have been an influence on the later half-dragon, half-turtle figure of Bixi in imperial Chinese sculpture. Bixi was considered a son of the Dragon King who was able to carry enormous weights upon his back; figures of the dragon-turtle bearing memorial stelae are common monuments throughout East Asia.

claims.statement: In Giles's translation of the Liezi, Nüwa cut off the legs of the Ao and used them to support the four corners of the heavens; Giles adds that this Chinese "Atlas" was a gigantic sea-turtle.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Liezi oleh Giles, Nüwa memotong kaki Ao dan memakainya menyangga empat sudut langit; Giles menambahkan bahwa "Atlas" Tiongkok ini adalah penyu laut raksasa.
claims.quote: He cut off the legs of the Ao and used them to support the four corners of the heavens. This Chinese “ Atlas ” was a gigantic sea-turtle.

claims.statement: The Kangxi Dictionary quotes the Shuowen that the ao (鼇) is a great turtle in the sea; the Yupian that a divine ao carries Mount Penglai on its back in the sea; and the Sanhuang Benji that Nüwa cut off the ao's feet to set up the four poles. The dictionary regards the writing 鰲 as a popular but incorrect form.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Kangxi mengutip Shuowen bahwa ao (鼇) adalah kura-kura besar di laut; Yupian menyebut ao yang bergaib memikul gunung Penglai di punggungnya di laut; dan Sanhuang Benji menyebut Nüwa memotong kaki ao untuk menegakkan empat tiang. Kamus ini menilai penulisan 鰲 sebagai bentuk umum yang tidak tepat.
claims.quote: 《說文》海中大鱉也。《玉篇》傳曰：有神靈之鼇，背負蓬萊之山，在海中。《史記·三皇本紀》女媧氏斷鼇足，以立四極。俗作鰲，非是。

claims.statement: According to this article, place names referring to an ao are more characteristic of China's southeastern coast (Zhejiang to Guangdong), including the Ao River (Aojiang) in southern Zhejiang and the Liu'ao ("Six ao") peninsula in southern Fujian.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, nama tempat yang memuat ao lebih khas di pesisir tenggara Tiongkok (Zhejiang hingga Guangdong), termasuk Sungai Ao (Aojiang) di Zhejiang selatan dan semenanjung Liu'ao ("Enam ao") di Fujian selatan.
claims.quote: place names referring to an ao are more characteristic of China's southeastern coast (Zhejiang to Guangdong). This includes the Ao River (Aojiang) in southern Zhejiang, with the town of Aojiang on its northern shore, as well as the Liu'ao ("Six ao") peninsula in southern Fujian.

claims.statement: Gwisin are spirits of dead people in Korean folklore, distinct from dokkaebi.
claims.statement_id: Gwisin adalah roh orang mati dalam cerita rakyat Korea, berbeda dari dokkaebi.
claims.quote: In Korean folklore, Gwisin (Korean: 귀신) are a type of deity, divinity, spirit or ghost. They are considered similar to a yogoe (Korean: 요괴) or mamul (Korean: 마물). Unlike dokkaebi, gwisin are humans who have died.

claims.statement: Ties to the living, such as revenge or care for loved ones, may keep a spirit on earth.
claims.statement_id: Ikatan dengan dunia hidup, seperti balas dendam atau menjaga orang tersayang, dapat menahan roh di bumi.
claims.quote: According to folklore, gwisin may be found in many places. It is claimed that when an individual dies but still has ties to the world of the living, such as in the case of revenge or caring for a loved one, their spirit remains on earth to complete the task before going on to the underworld.

claims.statement: Revenge is a common theme in gwisin tales.
claims.statement_id: Balas dendam menjadi tema umum cerita tentang gwisin.
claims.quote: There are a lot of legends about gwisin. Because they are a common form of ghost, children often make them up to scare others or parents tell stories to their children to teach them a lesson. The most common plot of a legend about gwisin is revenge, for example revenge for the family of the ghost. Another popular trope includes men who cheat on their wives, and murder someone.

claims.statement: Cheonyeo-gwisin is the spirit of a woman who died unmarried.
claims.statement_id: Cheonyeo-gwisin adalah roh perempuan yang meninggal tanpa menikah.
claims.quote: The Cheonyeo-gwisin (처녀귀신) is the gwisin of a woman who died unmarried and usually have white Hanbok (한복) which are worn for funerals.

claims.statement: Mul-gwisin is the spirit of a drowned person.
claims.statement_id: Mul-gwisin adalah roh orang yang tenggelam.
claims.quote: The Mul-gwisin (물귀신) is the spirit of someone who drowned.

claims.statement: According to the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, gwisin (귀신) is a divine being regarded as exercising superhuman or supernatural power; the concept is highly complex and divides broadly into pantheistic gwisin and saryeong (사령), the souls of the dead.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Ensiklopedia Kebudayaan Korea, gwisin (귀신) adalah sosok ilahi (神) yang dianggap memiliki kemampuan melampaui manusia atau alam; konsepnya sangat kompleks dan terbagi besar menjadi gwisin panteistik dan saryeong (사령), yaitu jiwa orang mati.
claims.quote: 귀신은 초인간적 또는 초자연적 능력을 발휘하는 주체로 여겨지는 신이다. 귀신이라는 개념은 매우 복합성을 지니고 있어서 다양한 대상을 지칭하여 사용된다. 크게 범신론적인 귀신, 죽은 자의 넋을 지칭하는 사령 두 가지로 나뉜다.

claims.statement: According to the encyclopedia, in a narrower sense gwisin also refers to the soul of a dead person, that is, saryeong (死靈) or saryeonggwi.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ensiklopedia itu, dalam arti sempit gwisin juga menunjuk jiwa orang yang telah meninggal, yaitu saryeong (死靈) atau saryeonggwi.
claims.quote: 그러나 좁은 뜻으로 쓰일 때는 죽은 이의 넋, 곧 사령(死靈) 또는 사령귀를 지칭하기도 하는 말이다.

claims.statement: According to the encyclopedia, if any one of three conditions is lacking the gwisin becomes a wollyeong (怨靈) or wongwi (寃鬼), and people feel fear and try to keep a respectful distance from it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ensiklopedia itu, jika salah satu dari tiga syarat kekurangan, gwisin menjadi wollyeong (怨靈) atau wongwi (寃鬼), dan orang merasa takut serta berusaha menjauhinya dengan hormat.
claims.quote: 하지만 세 가지 조건 중에서 어느 것 하나만 결격이 되어도 귀신은 이른바 원령(怨靈) 내지 원귀(寃鬼)가 된다. 사람들은 두려움을 느끼면서 그것을 경이원지(敬而遠之)하려 든다.

claims.statement: According to the encyclopedia, a wongwi is the soul of a dead person that cannot go to the afterlife and wanders this world.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ensiklopedia itu, wongwi adalah jiwa orang mati yang tidak dapat pergi ke alam baka dan mengembara di dunia ini.
claims.quote: 원귀는 죽은 이의 넋으로, 저승에 가지 못하고 이승을 헤매고 있는 떠돌이 넋이다.

claims.statement: The encyclopedia names three kinds of ghosts of the underage: the maiden ghost (처녀귀신) called "sonmalmyeong", the bachelor ghost (총각귀신) also called "mongdal-gwisin", and the baby ghost (아기귀신) called "gongjini" or "taejagwi" for those who died as infants.
claims.statement_id: Ensiklopedia itu menyebut tiga hantu di bawah umur: cheonyeo-gwisin (처녀귀신) yang disebut "sonmalmyeong", hantu bujangan (총각귀신) yang disebut "mongdal-gwisin", dan hantu bayi (아기귀신) yang disebut "gongjini" atau "taejagwi" untuk yang meninggal saat bayi.
claims.quote: 이른바 ‘손말명’이라고 불리는 처녀귀신, ‘몽달귀신’이라 불리기도 하는 총각귀신, 그리고 유아로 죽은 ‘공진이’ 또는 ‘태자귀’라는 이름의 아기귀신 등 3대미성년귀신

claims.statement: According to the encyclopedia, most ancestral spirits (조상귀신) are the typical gwisin that satisfy all three conditions; they are revered as sacred gwisin and descendants expect hidden blessings (eumdeok) from them.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ensiklopedia itu, sebagian besar roh leluhur (조상귀신) adalah contoh khas gwisin yang memenuhi ketiga syarat; mereka dihormati sebagai gwisin yang suci dan keturunannya mengharapkan berkah tersembunyi dari mereka.
claims.quote: 대부분의 조상령, 곧 조상귀신은 세 조건을 고루 갖춘 귀신의 전형이다. 이들은 거룩한 귀신으로서 떠받듦을 받고 후손들은 그에게서 이른바 음덕을 기대하게 된다.

claims.statement: The Four Holy Beasts are a group of Chinese auspicious creatures mentioned in the Book of Rites.
claims.statement_id: Four Holy Beasts adalah kelompok makhluk bertuah Tiongkok yang disebut dalam Kitab Ritus.
claims.quote: The Four Holy Beasts (Chinese: 四靈、四聖獸、or 四大神獸) are Chinese astronomical and cultural Four Benevolent Animals that are spread in the East Asian cultural sphere. They are mentioned in the Chinese classic Book of Rites and includes the Dragon (龍) in the East, the Qilin (麟) in the West, the Turtle (龜) in the North, and the Fenghuang (鳳) in the South.

claims.statement: Its members are dragon, qilin, turtle, and fenghuang.
claims.statement_id: Anggotanya ialah naga, qilin, kura-kura, dan fenghuang.
claims.quote: The Four Holy Beasts (Chinese: 四靈、四聖獸、or 四大神獸) are Chinese astronomical and cultural Four Benevolent Animals that are spread in the East Asian cultural sphere. They are mentioned in the Chinese classic Book of Rites and includes the Dragon (龍) in the East, the Qilin (麟) in the West, the Turtle (龜) in the North, and the Fenghuang (鳳) in the South.

claims.statement: This group differs from the Four Symbols, which include White Tiger.
claims.statement_id: Kelompok ini dibedakan dari Four Symbols, yang mencakup Harimau Putih.
claims.quote: The Four Holy Beasts differs from  Four Symbols in that Qilin replaces the White Tiger.  The Four Symbols are the Azure Dragon (青龍) in the East, White Tiger (白虎) in the West, Vermilion Bird (朱雀) in the South, and the Black Turtle-Snake (玄武) in the North.

claims.statement: Patterns of this group occur on Goryeo bronze mirrors and pottery.
claims.statement_id: Pola kelompok ini ditemukan pada cermin perunggu Goryeo dan tembikar.
claims.quote: Patterns of the four holy beasts are found in Bronze mirrors of the Goryeo dynasty and Pottery.

claims.statement: The Liji (chapter Liyun) asks "what are the four ling (四靈)?" and answers: the qilin (麟), the fenghuang (鳳), the tortoise (龜), and the dragon (龍).
claims.statement_id: Liji (bab Liyun) bertanya "apa yang disebut empat ling (四靈)?" dan menjawab: qilin (麟), fenghuang (鳳), kura-kura (龜), dan naga (龍).
claims.quote: 四靈以爲畜，故飲食有由也。何謂四靈？麟、鳳、龜、龍，謂之四靈。

claims.statement: The Liji states that when the dragon is taken as a kept animal (畜) the fish are not startled, when the fenghuang is, the birds are not startled, when the qilin is, the beasts are not startled, and when the tortoise is, human feelings do not go astray.
claims.statement_id: Liji menyatakan bahwa bila naga dijadikan hewan peliharaan (畜) ikan tidak terusik, bila fenghuang demikian burung tidak terusik, bila qilin demikian hewan buas tidak terusik, dan bila kura-kura demikian perasaan manusia tidak keliru.
claims.quote: 故龍以爲畜，故魚鮪不淰；鳳以爲畜，故鳥不獝；麟以爲畜，故獸不狘；龜以爲畜，故人情不失。
